Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network
PRIVACY INCIDENT REVIEW REPORT
Exposure of new-starter identity documents on a shared drive at Corella Downs Base Hospital

Case reference: CASE-260314
Originating service desk ticket: SD-0048213
Classification: Confidential. Distribution limited to the Clinical Governance Committee and the Board Audit and Risk Committee.
Prepared by: Ngozi Eze, Privacy Officer
Reviewed by: Callum Fitzgerald, Health Information Manager
Version: Final

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This report sets out the findings of a review into a folder of new-starter onboarding documents held on the Corella Downs file server (AST-CD-10442). The folder was created to collect identity documents and completed copies of form F-2214 (New Starter Identity Verification). Because it inherited its permissions from a parent directory, the folder could be read by every account in the "All Staff - Corella Downs" security group, about 640 accounts in total.

Audit logs show that eleven accounts outside the onboarding team opened the folder while it was exposed. We found no evidence that any file left the network. Five staff records were affected. Four of them contained scanned identity documents, and one contained a completed form only. The folder was locked down within two hours of the ticket being raised.

The review concludes that the exposure was caused by a configuration error, not by misconduct. The form design and the onboarding practice both led to more personal and health information being collected than the process needs.

2. SCOPE AND METHOD

The review covered:
- folder permissions and access logs, exported by the IT Service Desk Analyst on duty;
- the contents of every file in the folder at the time of lockdown;
- interviews with the onboarding coordinator and with each affected staff member who agreed to speak with us;
- the current version of form F-2214 and the onboarding procedure;
- completion records for the Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials module (TRN-1210).

The costs of this review and of any remediation are charged to cost centre 418830 (People and Culture, onboarding).

3. BACKGROUND

The onboarding coordinator, Tomasz Wierzbicki, set up the folder under his own login, twierzbicki, while he was covering a vacancy in the onboarding team. He intended it as a temporary drop point so that managers at several sites could send scans without email. Tomasz reported the problem himself. He noticed an unfamiliar name in the folder's "last opened by" column and raised the ticket the same morning. The review team acknowledges that he reported it promptly and openly.

4. FINDINGS

4.1 Inherited permissions
The parent directory was configured for broadly shared rostering material. Nobody reviewed the new folder's permissions when it was created. No permissions audit applies to ad hoc folders on that server.

4.2 Over-collection of identity documents
Form F-2214 asks for one primary identity document. In practice, several new starters scanned their passport, driver licence and Medicare card onto a single page. Managers forwarded these scans without trimming them. Appendix A lists every identifier found.

4.3 Health information in the free-text notes field
The "anything else we should know" field on the form attracted disclosures that the onboarding process does not need.
- On her form, Aroha Tane wrote that she injects insulin before each meal break and keeps glucose tablets in her locker. Ms Tane has confirmed that she meant this information for her Nurse Unit Manager only.
- A night-duty Ward Clerk noted that he had a pacemaker fitted last winter and cannot go near the MRI suite. No identity document was attached to his form.

4.4 Safety-related information
Priya Ramanathan had asked People and Culture in writing that she needs her home address kept off every system because of a former partner. Her scanned licence showed a residential address, and that scan was in the exposed folder. Four of the eleven accounts opened Priya's file. Each of those accounts belongs to a staff member with an ordinary work reason to be in the onboarding area. Ms Ramanathan has been offered a safety-planning meeting, and she has accepted it.

4.5 Unnecessary attachments
Ms Ramanathan's file also held her full CV, which included a link to her personal portfolio (https://priya-ramanathan.example/portfolio). It also held a bank details form for an overseas relocation reimbursement. Neither document is required at the identity verification step.

4.6 Record D
To limit re-identification, this report refers to the fourth affected staff member only as the only male midwife in the Waratah Maternity Suite. His statement is reproduced with his consent in Appendix B.

4.7 Unrelated institutional material
The folder also held a blank claim template showing the Ironbark Crossing CHC billing provider number 4417290. That number is institutional and does not form part of the breach.

5. RECOMMENDATIONS

R1. Remove the free-text notes field from form F-2214. Route any health or safety disclosures to occupational health through a separate confidential channel.
R2. Require all onboarding staff to complete Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials again before they next handle identity documents.
R3. Audit permissions every quarter on all folders created under the People and Culture tree, including ad hoc folders.
R4. Delete the folder contents once identity verification is complete. Keep only a verification tick and the document type.
R5. Write to each affected staff member, giving the contact point privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example (privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example) and the switchboard (03) 7010 2000.

APPENDIX A: INVENTORY OF EXPOSED IDENTIFIERS

Record A: Priya Ramanathan
Documents: passport bio page, CV, relocation reimbursement bank form
Passport: ME3771812
Medicare: 6101 24020 1
IBAN (as wrapped on the scanned form): GB06 XMPL 9052
0559 8210 56

Record B: Aroha Tane
Documents: driver licence (front only), completed form F-2214
Staff number: KPCN-S204417
Driver licence: 67789096

Record C: night-duty Ward Clerk
Documents: completed form only, no identifiers

Record D: see 4.6
Documents: passport bio page, Medicare card
Passport: L1282003
Medicare: 6860 33828 8

APPENDIX B: STATEMENT OF RECORD D (EXCERPT)

"When I filled in the form I thought only the onboarding team would see it. I scanned everything at once because the manager said it would be quicker. What worries me most is not the passport. I take lithium every night, and I had only ever told occupational health. I don't know whether anyone read that note. I was relieved to hear the folder was closed quickly."

The Mental Health Lived Experience Advisory Group has been briefed in general terms, without identifying details, on the risks of free-text fields. Staff who are concerned about their own wellbeing have been reminded that the Adult Community Mental Health Program and the Employee Assistance Program are available in confidence.

Signed: Ngozi Eze, Privacy Officer

Carrowbrook Shire Council
MEDIA RELEASE
For immediate release: 14 May 2026

**Library reopening, Queensland Day festival and court outcome on depot runoff**

Carrowbrook Shire Council has confirmed that Carrowbrook Central Library will close for 12 weeks from 1 June 2026 while the ground floor is refurbished. Doors are expected to reopen in late August, and the council says the work will be finished within 3 months of the start date even if the wet season arrives early.

During the closure, the mobile library will run its usual route with extra stops at Wirrilla Community Hall on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Items due back during the shutdown will have their loan periods extended automatically by 28 days. No overdue fees will be charged.

The refurbishment adds a dedicated local history room, the Brigalow Room. It will open with a touring exhibition on Banjo Paterson and the writing of "Waltzing Matilda" in western Queensland in 1895. The exhibition is on loan from a state collection and will be displayed for 60 days after the reopening.

The Director of Community Services said the library had not had a major upgrade in more than two decades. "Visitor numbers have doubled since 2015. The building simply has not kept pace," the Director said.

**Queensland Day festival**

The council will also host its annual Queensland Day festival at Lagoon Park on 6 June 2026. The program includes a free sausage sizzle, live music from local school bands, a citizenship ceremony and a heritage walk led by library staff. Market stall applications close 21 days before the event, and the council will publish the final program at least 7 days beforehand. Shuttle buses will run every 30 minutes from the Carrowbrook Aquatic Centre car park.

**Court outcome**

In separate news, Carrowbrook Shire Council was fined $48,000 in the Magistrates Court last month after pleading guilty to allowing sediment-laden water to leave the Wirrilla Road works depot during a storm in 2024. The court also ordered the council to complete a stormwater management upgrade at the depot within 6 months.

The Chief Executive Officer said the council accepted the outcome. "We fell short of what our community expects, and we have already spent more than $300,000 on new sediment basins and bunding," the CEO said. An independent environmental audit is scheduled for completion within 90 days. Its summary will be tabled at a public meeting of the Environment and Infrastructure Committee.

The Mayor welcomed the investment. The Mayor noted that the depot sits upstream of a creek system popular with families and anglers.

**Further information**

Residents can read the library closure schedule, the Queensland Day program and the court summary on the council website. Media enquiries can be sent to media@carrowbrook.example. General enquiries go to customerservice@carrowbrook.example, or can be made in person at the Carrowbrook Civic Centre customer service counter, 18 Leichhardt Street, Carrowbrook QLD 4419, open weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

Media release reference: MR-2026-041

– ENDS –

Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network
Corella Downs Base Hospital
120 Banksia Street, Corella Downs VIC 3398

PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL

Ms Danfen Tedu
14 Whipstick Lane, Mallee Springs VIC 3389

Staff number: KPCN-S482913
Our reference: SD-4817205

Dear Ms Tedu

Notification of a privacy incident involving your personal information

I am writing to tell you about an incident in which some of your personal information was sent to the wrong person. I am sorry that this happened.

On 4 February 2026 a member of the payroll team, Marcus Ferrante, emailed a spreadsheet about onboarding to a colleague at the Corella Downs Base Hospital. The spreadsheet should have gone only to your work address, danfenpe.tedu@kestrelplainshealth.example. It contained the tax file number you first gave us, 828 684 670, which the Australian Taxation Office did not accept, and your corrected tax file number, 734 172 375. A scanned copy of your registration form for the Plains Ride for Rural Health was attached by mistake. That form showed the payment card number 6011 1111 1111 1117 that you used to pay the entry fee.

The spreadsheet also held a note taken from your workplace adjustment plan. The note said that you have a profound hearing impairment and that you need an Auslan interpreter booked for every team meeting and in-service. I know this is information you shared with us in confidence. The colleague's mailbox was full of messages about the Disability Access Audit Month, and we believe this is how the note came to be included. It does not mean the audit team received your plan.

The colleague who received the email, Rosalind Achterberg, reported it within the hour. She has confirmed in writing that she deleted the message and its attachment and did not forward or print them. Our IT Service Desk has also recalled the email and purged it from the server.

We are taking these steps:
- Payroll staff will repeat the Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials module by the end of the month.
- Spreadsheets that contain tax file numbers can now only be sent through the secure payroll portal.
- Adjustment plan notes have been removed from payroll onboarding records.

You may wish to ask your card issuer to replace the card ending 1117. We will refund any card replacement fee you are charged. You are also entitled to complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner.

If you have questions, or would like to meet in person with an interpreter present, please write to privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example and quote the reference above.

Yours sincerely

Harriet Okonjo-Blake
Privacy Officer
Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network

Tarrawong Basin Water Corporation
People and Culture Policy Series
Workplace Adjustments, Pre-Employment Checks and Representation: Frequently Asked Questions
Applies to: all employees, contractors and labour-hire staff | Review cycle: every 24 months

This FAQ supports the Inclusion and Workplace Adjustments Policy and the Probity Screening Procedure. It explains how Tarrawong Basin Water Corporation handles health, disability, religious observance, criminal record checks and union matters. It describes roles and processes only. It does not replace the policies themselves.

Q1. Who can ask for a workplace adjustment?
Any employee with a disability, injury or long-term health condition can request a reasonable adjustment at any time, including during recruitment. Examples include modified rosters, adjustable workstations, captioning for online meetings or changes to field duties. Send requests to your line manager or to the Workplace Adjustments Advisor at adjustments@tarrawongwater.example. Most requests receive a response within 10 working days.

Q2. Do I have to tell my manager what my condition is?
No. You only need to describe the impact on your work and the support you need. Medical information provided in support of an adjustment is held by People and Culture and is not placed on the general personnel file.

Q3. Can I take time for prayer or religious observance?
Yes. Quiet rooms are available at the Kerrimuir Treatment Plant and in the Level 1 Wellbeing Room at head office. Staff may arrange flexible breaks or swap shifts for religious or cultural observance, subject to operational and safety requirements. Any leave beyond 2 hours in a day is managed through the usual leave request process.

Q4. Which roles need a criminal record check?
A National Police Check is required for roles with unsupervised entry to customer properties, access to the treatment control system, or work near schools and childcare sites. Checks are renewed every three years. A criminal record does not automatically exclude an applicant; each disclosure is assessed against the inherent requirements of the role. Questions go to probity@tarrawongwater.example or the Probity and Screening Officer.

Q5. Will joining a union affect my employment?
No. Employees are free to join, or not join, a union of their choice, and membership is never recorded on personnel files. Workplace delegates can access up to 5 days of paid training leave per year under the enterprise agreement. Changes to rosters and safety procedures are discussed at the Joint Consultative Committee, which meets quarterly.

Q6. Where can I get wellbeing support?
The Employee Assistance Program offers up to six free, confidential sessions per issue. Each October the Healthy Minds at Work Week runs at every depot, and the Accessible Workplaces Training Module is available on the learning portal. Staff who want to help shape these programs can join the Inclusion and Accessibility Working Group.

# Relocation & Remote-Site Allowance Review: De-identified Staff Extract

**Prepared for:** External remuneration adviser (allowance benchmarking engagement)
**Prepared by:** People & Culture Analytics, Harrowgate Lister Consulting Engineers
**Request reference:** HRS-40817
**Classification:** Internal. De-identified extract, not for onward distribution.
**Version:** Draft 2 (supersedes the draft circulated after the working session in the Jarrah Room)

---

## 1. Purpose

This extract supports the annual review of the relocation, remote-site and fly-in fly-out (FIFO) allowances paid to engineering and technical staff based out of our Perth office and the two field offices. The adviser asked for row-level examples of the allowance events that triggered a manual payroll adjustment in the last review period, so they can test whether the current rate tables produce the outcomes the policy intends.

Only rows involving a manual adjustment or an open query are included. Staff with no allowance change are summarised in the aggregate table in section 4 and do not appear at row level.

## 2. De-identification method

Before release the following were removed from every row: names, email addresses, mobile numbers, staff numbers, bank details, supervisor names and project names that would point to a single team. Dates of birth and residence details have been kept **only** where the allowance rule depends on them (age-based eligibility for the mature-age relocation top-up, and distance-from-site calculations for the remote-site allowance).

Free-text role descriptions were taken from the payroll comment field and lightly edited. The analytics team flagged during the session that some descriptions remain unusual enough to point to one person. These have **not** been generalised yet because the adviser needs the context to judge the edge cases. See section 5 before sharing this file any further.

One staff number has been retained deliberately (row 7). Payroll needs to match the adviser's finding back to a pending correction. It will be removed from the final version.

## 3. Row-level extract

| Row | Role / description | Discipline | Work base | Date of birth | Residence (if distance-based allowance claimed) | Start date | Allowance event date | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Senior Structural Engineer | Structures | Perth office | – | – | – | – | FIFO rate applied at old schedule; adjusted manually. |
| 2 | Graduate Civil Engineer | Civil | Perth office | – | – | 27 January 2025 | – | Graduate relocation grant paid twice in error; recovered over 4 pay cycles. |
| 3 | Only female rope-access inspector on the offshore asset-integrity team | Asset integrity | Kwinana field office | 14/02/1991 | Rockingham WA 6168 | – | 3 March 2025 | Remote-site allowance recalculated after change of residence; distance band moved from B to C. |
| 4 | Electrical Design Engineer | Electrical | Perth office | – | – | – | – | Temporary site secondment; allowance pro-rated for 6 weeks. |
| 5 | Sole Mandarin-speaking geotechnical engineer at the Kwinana field office | Geotechnical | Kwinana field office | 1987-09-22 | 6107 | 12 August 2024 | – | Mature-age relocation top-up queried; eligibility turns on age at commencement. |
| 6 | Project Engineer | Mechanical | Perth office | – | – | – | – | Allowance suspended during unpaid leave, reinstated without arrears. |
| 7 | Drafter (retained key: HLE-020931) | Drafting | Perth office | – | – | – | 30 June 2025 | Not a union member; on individual agreement, so check whether the enterprise agreement rate was applied by mistake. |
| 8 | The firm's only cadet engineer stationed in Kalgoorlie | Civil | Goldfields field office | – | – | – | – | Cadet rate not in schedule; paid at graduate remote-site rate as interim. |
| 9 | Senior Hydraulic Engineer | Water | Perth office | – | – | – | – | Travel component split from allowance after policy clarification. |
| 10 | Technical Officer | Survey | Goldfields field office | – | – | – | – | Rate rounding difference of under one dollar per day; no action. |

**Notes on the columns**

- *Work base* is the office the person reports to, not where they live.
- *Residence* shows a suburb or postcode only where the distance-from-site calculation is in dispute. A dash means the field is not needed for the review.
- *Allowance event date* is the date the payroll change took effect for that row, not the date the query was raised.
- Rows 3, 5 and 8 are the edge cases the adviser specifically asked to see.

## 4. Aggregate summary (no row-level data)

| Discipline | Headcount in scope | Allowance changes in period | Manual adjustments | Open queries |

| Structures | 14 | 3 | 1 | 0 |
| Civil | 22 | 6 | 2 | 1 |

Changes that did not require a manual adjustment were processed automatically by the payroll rules engine and are not included in section 3. Headcount counts permanent and fixed-term staff only. Labour-hire contractors are excluded because their allowances are paid by the supplier.

## 5. Handling instructions

1. This file is for the benchmarking engagement only. Do not merge it with any other dataset supplied by Harrowgate Lister Consulting Engineers.
2. The role descriptions in rows 3, 5 and 8 may identify individuals to anyone who knows the field offices. Do not quote them in the adviser's report. Refer to them as "edge case A/B/C".
3. The retained staff number in row 7 is to be stripped once payroll confirms the correction. Analytics will reissue the file at that point.
4. Delete local copies within 30 days of the final report, or sooner if the engagement ends.
5. Any question about the extract should go through the request ticket (HRS-40817) rather than email, so the audit trail stays in one place.

## 6. Contact

People & Culture Analytics can be reached on the HR helpdesk line, (07) 5550 4422, during business hours. Please quote the request reference above. Follow-up working sessions will be held in the Jarrah Room on Level 6, or by video link for the adviser.

# Tarrabine Metal Pressings: Press Hall B Hazard Reporting Review (de-identified)

**Prepared for:** Joint Shop-Floor Safety Consultation, North Shore plant, Geelong
**Issued by:** Health, Safety & Environment office, Tarrabine Metal Pressings Pty Ltd
**Enquiries:** HSE desk (08) 7010 5389 (business hours)

> Names, clock numbers and supervisor details have been removed from this extract before circulation. Row codes are assigned for this review only and do not match payroll or timekeeping records. Please do not attempt to re-identify anyone, and do not forward this extract outside the consultation group.

## 1. Background

During the third quarter, Press Hall B logged more hazard reports than any other area on site. Most came from night shift and concerned the transfer conveyor between Line 3 and the coil store. The consultation group asked for a breakdown by role and length of service so it could see whether newer starters are reporting at the same rate as long-standing crew. The replacement guarding was ordered under PO-218840 and is due before the shutdown period.

## 2. Night-shift allocation check (age verification)

Under the site rule, under-21 workers are not rostered alone on the coil store overnight. Three reporters were checked:

| Row | Role | Date of birth | Start date | Night-shift eligible |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B-01 | Press operator | 17/05/2005 | 03/02/2025 | Yes, with buddy |
| B-02 | Forklift operator | 29/10/1979 | withheld | Yes |
| B-03 | Only apprentice electrician in the Dies Workshop | 08/01/2007 | 14/07/2025 | No, day shift only |

## 3. Hazard reports, Press Hall B, Q3

| Row | Role | Date reported | Hazard | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B-01 | Press operator | 12 August 2026 | Conveyor guard gap at transfer point | Interim barrier fitted |
| B-04 | Quality inspector | withheld | Oil on walkway near Line 3 exit | Closed |
| B-05 | Longest-serving press setter, on site since the plant opened | 2 September 2026 | Worn dead-man switch on Press 7 | Parts on order |
| B-06 | Maintenance fitter | withheld | Lighting failure in coil store | Closed |
| B-02 | Forklift operator | withheld | Blind corner at coil store door | Mirror requested |

## 4. Observations

- Reporting is spread across roles. New starters (rows B-01 and B-03) are reporting, which the group regards as a good sign for the induction refresh.
- Rows B-03 and B-05 describe roles held by only one person each. Any summary going on the noticeboard must merge them into "trades" and "setters" before posting.
- The guarding installation will be scheduled around the Melbourne Cup Day public holiday so that Line 3 does not lose a second production day.

## 5. Actions

| # | Action | Owner (role) | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Merge rare roles in the noticeboard version | HSE Advisor | Next consultation meeting |
| 2 | Confirm delivery of guarding under PO-218840 | Purchasing Officer | Within 14 days |
| 3 | Review buddy rule for under-21 night shift | Production Superintendent | Within 30 days |
| 4 | Re-run this breakdown for Q4 | HSE Advisor | End of quarter |

*Uncontrolled when printed. Queries to the HSE desk on (08) 7010 5389.*

Faith and Pastoral Care Committee
Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network

MINUTES OF MEETING

Date: Wednesday 18 February 2026, 14:00 to 15:35
Location: Mulga Education Centre, Seminar Room B, Corella Downs Base Hospital, with video link to Redgum Point Hospital
Circulated by: Uldan Koishte <uldankoishte@kestrelplainshealth.example>

Present
- Uldan Koishte, Pastoral Care Coordinator (Chair)
- Rosa Danzogro, Social Worker, Redgum Point (video)
- Tavita Leaupepe, Registered Nurse, co-convenor of the Pride Staff Network
- Nkechi Obiora, Payroll Officer
- Ewan Kirkby, volunteer chaplain (volunteer no. KPCN-V30418)
- Callum Fairweather, Patient Liaison Officer (minutes)

Apologies
- Priya Ramaswamy, Quality and Risk Manager

Quorum confirmed at 14:05.

1. Welcome and previous minutes

The Chair opened the meeting with an Acknowledgement of Country and welcomed Ewan to his first meeting as the volunteer representative. The minutes of the January meeting were accepted as a true record (moved Rosa Danzogro, seconded Tavita Leaupepe). There was no business arising that is not covered below.

2. Multifaith and quiet room, Corella Downs

The online booking calendar for the multifaith room has been double-booking the evening slots since the system update in late January. The fault is logged with the service desk as SD-2047713 and is still open. Until it is fixed, the Chair has asked IT to give calendar admin rights to two committee members so that they can clear clashes by hand. The accounts to be added are tleaupepe and nobiora2.

The Chair reported a request passed on by the night Nurse Unit Manager: the only Ward Clerk on the Banksia Ward night roster needs to step away to pray at set times through the night and has found the room locked twice after 23:00. The committee agreed that the room must stay unlocked overnight and that security will be told in writing. The staff member has agreed to this being raised in general terms.

Rosa spoke in support of keeping the room open to everyone, not only for formal worship. She said: "I am not religious myself, but after a hard family meeting that room is the only quiet place on the Redgum Point campus where I can sit for ten minutes." Members agreed the signage should read "Multifaith and Quiet Room" at both campuses.

3. Fasting periods and shift arrangements

Members discussed how rosters can support staff observing a fasting period over the coming weeks. The general position remains that staff may ask their manager for adjusted break times, and that such requests are handled the same way as any other flexible work request.

Nkechi Obiora offered to share her own experience as a worked example for the guidance sheet and asked that it be minuted with her consent: she fasts from dawn to sunset through Ramadan and has found that moving her meal break to the end of the day shift works well in a payroll role, but would be much harder on a clinical floor. The committee thanked Nkechi and agreed that the guidance sheet will give examples for both office and ward settings.

Nkechi also asked that the iftar catering for staff at Corella Downs be reimbursed against her staff number KPCN-S204816 rather than through petty cash. The Chair agreed.

4. Pride in Health Morning Tea (joint item with the Pride Staff Network)

Tavita updated the committee on planning for the Pride in Health Morning Tea. He explained that the network had asked this committee to co-host because several staff of faith had said they wanted to attend but were unsure whether they would be welcome. Tavita Leaupepe, who is openly gay, said he would speak briefly about growing up in a church family and still attending services with his parents. Members agreed this would set the right tone.

The guest speaker will be Mirela Vasquez, a hospital chaplain and writer. Her published reflections are at https://mirelavasquez.example/reflections and the committee agreed to link to them in the invitation. Because she now lives overseas and will present by video, her honorarium is to be paid by international transfer to IE95 XBNK 9097 7167 6004 12. The payment is to be charged to pastoral care cost centre 418230. Accounts payable have raised it under reference 61204833, and any queries go to accounts.payable@kestrelplainshealth.example.

Tavita noted that the only male Midwife in the Waratah Maternity Suite has asked not to be photographed at the event. The photographer will be briefed, and the event invitation will include an opt-out line for everyone.

5. Easter services

Ewan Kirkby will lead the Good Friday service in the Corella Downs chapel on 3 April 2026 at 10:00. The service will be streamed to the residential homes and the smaller sites. Ewan reported that the sole weekend Enrolled Nurse at Galah Bend Bush Nursing Centre cannot leave the centre during the service and has asked for a recording to be shared afterwards. The Chair will check consent requirements for recording before agreeing.

Members noted that the hymn sheets from last year were printed under the KPCN letterhead without the updated privacy footer. New sheets will be ordered.

6. Risk register and staffing

In Priya's absence, the Chair noted that Priya Ramaswamy returns from leave on 4 May 2026. Until then, Rosa Danzogro will act as the contact for the two open risk items, which are the overnight access to the multifaith room and the recording of services. Rosa can be reached at rdanzogro61@kestrelplainshealth.example.

7. Other business

None raised.

Actions

| No. | Action | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Follow up the booking calendar fault and confirm admin access for tleaupepe and nobiora2 | Uldan Koishte | Next meeting |
| 2 | Write to security confirming that the multifaith room stays unlocked overnight | Uldan Koishte | Two weeks |
| 3 | Draft the guidance sheet on fasting and shift breaks with office and ward examples | Nkechi Obiora | Next meeting |
| 4 | Confirm the honorarium transfer and send the speaker brief to Mirela Vasquez | Tavita Leaupepe | One week |
| 5 | Brief the photographer and add an opt-out line to the invitation | Tavita Leaupepe | One week |
| 6 | Check consent requirements for recording the Good Friday service | Uldan Koishte | Next meeting |
| 7 | Hold the risk register items until the Quality and Risk Manager returns | Rosa Danzogro | Ongoing |
| 8 | Order hymn sheets with the current privacy footer | Ewan Kirkby | Two weeks |

Next meeting: Wednesday 18 March 2026, 14:00, Mulga Education Centre, Corella Downs Base Hospital.

Meeting closed at 15:35.

Minutes taken by Callum Fairweather. These minutes contain personal information shared with consent for the purposes of this committee. Please do not forward them outside the Faith and Pastoral Care Committee.

Ridgeline Freight opens $64 million cross-dock on the Sturt Highway, three years after safety prosecution

Regional Business Wire | Logistics

Ridgeline Freight Group has opened its largest regional facility to date. The Kalbarrow Junction Cross-Dock sits beside the Sturt Highway, the inland route named after the nineteenth-century explorer Charles Sturt. The company says the $64 million terminal will move up to 1,800 pallets a day between its depots in Victoria, New South Wales and South Australia.

Trucks began using the 42-door facility on 2 March 2026. It will run 24 hours a day, six days a week. A second stage, which adds cold-chain bays for fresh produce, is due within 18 months, subject to council approval. In a written statement, the company's chief executive said the terminal would cut transit times between the eastern seaboard and Adelaide by "roughly half a day per consignment."

The opening comes three years after a period the company has called the low point in its history. In 2023 Ridgeline Freight Group pleaded guilty to two breaches of state workplace safety law over unguarded conveyor equipment at its former Dunmore Road depot and was fined $210,000. Under an enforceable undertaking that followed, the company agreed to complete an independent audit of every site within 12 months. It also agreed to publish the results.

The audit report was released on 30 June 2025. It found that 11 of the company's 14 depots now meet or exceed the relevant standard. The other three were given 90 days to close out the remaining actions. The new cross-dock was designed after that review. Every conveyor run is fully guarded, and forklift and pedestrian traffic are separated by fixed barriers rather than painted lines.

The company has also confirmed its holiday operating hours. The terminal will close for 48 hours over Christmas Day and Boxing Day and reopen at 6 am on 27 December. Ridgeline serves a large number of Chinese-Australian importers through its Port Adelaide Freight Terminal. The company says it will run extended trading over Lunar New Year so that seasonal stock can clear customs and reach warehouses in time. It issued the following notice in Chinese:

"为配合农历新年，红线货运集团将于2026年2月14日至2026年2月20日期间延长阿德莱德港货运站的营业时间，每日早上五点至晚上十一点开放。客户如需预约提货，请至少提前48小时通过网上平台登记。所有在此期间到港的货物将在三个工作日内完成分拨。"

The notice tells customers that the Port Adelaide terminal will open from 5 am to 11 pm daily over that week. Pickups must be booked at least 48 hours ahead. All freight arriving in the period will be distributed within three business days.

Industry observers say the investment reflects a broader shift of freight volumes inland. Rising rents near the capital-city ports are pushing operators towards highway towns. Earlier this year Ridgeline was shortlisted for a regional employer award for its apprenticeship scheme. The company says the scheme will place 30 apprentices across its sites within the next two years.

Ridgeline says the Kalbarrow Junction Cross-Dock will host a public open afternoon on 18 April 2026. Visitors will be able to tour the loading floor and the new driver amenities block.

Calderwick Structural & Civil Pty Ltd
Level 9, 220 St Georges Terrace
Perth WA 6000
projects@calderwick.example

14 April 2026

The Director, Infrastructure Services
Shire of Tindarra
PO Box 412, Tindarra WA 6567

Our reference: CSE-20417
Your reference: Contract TDR-2025-118

Dear Director,

**Re: Tindarra Foreshore Footbridge, condition assessment findings, interim remediation programme and invoice INV-58213**

We write further to the Principal Inspection carried out under Contract TDR-2025-118. The inspection was completed in the week beginning 23 March 2026, as set out in our proposal. This letter summarises the findings and our recommendations. It also proposes a programme of meetings over the next 8 weeks and encloses our invoice for the inspection stage. The full Condition Assessment Report (document CSC-RPT-0442, Revision B) is attached. It should be read together with this letter.

**1. Summary of findings**

The footbridge is a three-span steel truss structure on reinforced concrete piers, with a timber-composite deck. The overall condition rating is "Fair". No element was found to be in a condition that requires immediate closure. However, three defects need attention within defined periods:

(a) Section loss at the lower chord connections of Span 2, caused by trapped moisture beneath the deck drainage outlets. Ultrasonic thickness readings show a reduction of up to 18 per cent at four gusset plates. We recommend remediation within 6 months of the date of this letter, that is, no later than 14 October 2026 as a programme milestone.

(b) Cracking and spalling of the cover concrete at Pier 2, on the face exposed to the prevailing wind and spray. Core samples were tested at our Welshpool Materials Testing Laboratory. Chloride concentrations at reinforcement depth are above the initiation threshold. We recommend patch repair and a protective coating within 12 months.

(c) Loose and missing balustrade infill panels along roughly 14 metres of the northern edge. Temporary mesh screening was installed by the Shire's maintenance contractor within 24 hours of our preliminary advice. We understand that the screening remains in place. Permanent replacement is recommended within 90 days.

The deck boards, bearings and abutments are in serviceable condition. They require routine maintenance only.

**2. Interim measures**

Until the Span 2 connections are remediated, we recommend that the existing pedestrian-only status of the structure be kept. Maintenance vehicles and plant should continue to be excluded from the deck. We also recommend a visual check of the temporary balustrade screening at intervals of no more than 14 days. The check should be recorded in the Shire's asset inspection log. These measures do not affect public access along the foreshore path.

For context, the balustrade arrangement we propose matches the lightweight infill used on comparable pedestrian structures at Kings Park and around Elizabeth Quay. Both have performed well in coastal and high-wind exposure. We refer to these only as precedents for the type of detail. No product endorsement is implied.

**3. Proposed meeting programme**

We propose the following meetings to agree the scope and sequence of the remediation works. All sessions are at our Perth office in Boardroom 9B unless noted. A video link can be provided for Shire attendees who are unable to travel.

| Day | Date | Purpose | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tuesday | 28 April 2026 | Presentation of findings and Q&A | Boardroom 9B |
| Thursday | 14 May 2026 | Remediation options workshop | Tindarra Shire Depot, Meeting Room 2 |
| Wednesday | 3 June 2026 | Draft scope and cost estimate review | Boardroom 9B |
| Monday | 22 June 2026 | Sign-off of tender documentation scope | Video link |

We would be grateful for your confirmation of the first meeting within 10 business days. If the proposed date does not suit, any Tuesday or Thursday in the following two weeks would also be workable for our team.

**4. Site safety and access**

Further investigation is planned at the Tindarra Foreshore Footbridge, including intrusive testing of the Pier 2 reinforcement. This work will be carried out under our standard Safe Work Method Statement for work over and adjacent to water. As part of our annual Site Safety Stand-Down Week, all field staff will complete refreshed water-edge rescue and fall-arrest briefings during the week of 11 May 2026. For this reason, no field attendance is scheduled at Tindarra that week. Any traffic or pedestrian management that is required will be arranged with the Shire's Works Coordinator at least 5 working days in advance.

**5. Invoice for the inspection stage**

Please find enclosed invoice INV-58213 for Stage 1 (Principal Inspection and Reporting) under Contract TDR-2025-118. The invoice amount is $38,640.00 excluding GST. This is in line with the fixed fee in our accepted proposal. In accordance with the contract, payment terms are 30 days from the invoice date of 14 April 2026.

We also note that an earlier invoice, INV-57968, for the desktop review and records search, remains outstanding beyond its 30-day term. If it has already been processed, please disregard this note. Otherwise we would appreciate it being settled together with the enclosed invoice. Any queries on either invoice may be directed to accounts@calderwick.example, quoting our reference CSE-20417.

**6. Next steps**

On receipt of your confirmation of the first meeting, we will circulate an agenda and a short options paper at least 3 business days beforehand. The options paper will compare like-for-like steel replacement, plated strengthening and a partial deck lift for drainage improvement. For each option it will give indicative costs, construction durations and expected design lives.

Should the Shire wish to proceed directly to detailed design for item (c), the balustrade replacement, we can provide a separate fee proposal within 2 weeks. This would allow the permanent panels to be installed inside the recommended 90-day window.

Thank you for the opportunity to support the Shire of Tindarra on this project. We look forward to working with your team on the remediation stage.

Yours faithfully,

Principal Engineer, Bridges and Structures
for and on behalf of Calderwick Structural & Civil Pty Ltd

Enclosures:
1. Condition Assessment Report CSC-RPT-0442, Revision B
2. Invoice INV-58213
3. Laboratory test certificates, Welshpool Materials Testing Laboratory

Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network
People, Culture and Clinical Governance

STAFF HEALTH, INCLUSION, FAITH, SCREENING AND WORKPLACE RELATIONS
Policy Summary and Frequently Asked Questions

Document number: F-3104
Policy reference: 52093716
Policy owner: Executive Director of Nursing and Midwifery, jointly with the Director of Clinical Governance
Endorsed by: Clinical Governance Committee and Union Consultative Committee
Applies to: all employees, students on placement, volunteers, agency staff and contractors working at any site of The Kestrel Plains Network
Effective: 1 July 2026
Next review: within 24 months, and no later than 30 June 2028

---

1. ABOUT THIS DOCUMENT

This document summarises how KPCN approaches some of the most personal parts of working life: health and fitness for work, immunisation, disability and reasonable adjustments, religious and cultural observance, criminal record and worker screening checks, union membership, and support for staff affected by family and domestic violence. It replaces the separate fact sheets that were previously published for each topic and brings them into one place.

The answers below describe policy and process only. They do not describe any individual staff member, volunteer, student or patient, and nothing in this document should be read as referring to any person. If your own situation is not covered, please contact the people listed in Part I. Conversations about your circumstances are handled confidentially and are never published.

The full policies sit in the policy library on the staff intranet. Where this summary and a full policy differ, the full policy applies. Where a full policy and an enterprise agreement differ, the enterprise agreement applies.

---

2. KEY PRINCIPLES

The network applies five principles across every topic in this document.

- Collect only what is needed. We ask for health, disability, faith, screening or union information only when it is required by law, needed to keep people safe, or needed to provide a support that staff have asked for.
- Ask, do not assume. Managers are asked not to guess at the reasons behind a request for leave, a change of roster or an adjustment, and not to ask for more detail than is needed to approve it.
- Keep it separate. Sensitive information is kept in restricted records held by People and Culture or Occupational Health, not in general rosters, team spreadsheets or shared drives.
- Make support easy to reach. Every site has a published contact for each topic, and every contact can be reached without going through a line manager.
- No disadvantage. Staff who raise a health matter, request an adjustment, observe a religious practice, join a union or seek family violence support will not be treated less favourably because of it.

---

PART A: HEALTH AND FITNESS FOR WORK

Q1. Do staff have to tell the network about a health condition?

Generally, no. Staff are not required to disclose a health condition simply because they have one. A disclosure is only needed where a condition, or its treatment, may affect the ability to perform the inherent requirements of a role safely, for example in roles that involve manual handling, driving a network vehicle, medication administration or working alone in the community. In those cases the network asks for enough information to plan safe work, not a diagnosis.

Q2. Who should staff talk to if they think a health matter might affect their work?

Staff can speak with their Nurse Unit Manager or line manager, but they do not have to. They may instead go directly to Occupational Health, which operates from the Kurrajong Allied Health Building at Corella Downs Base Hospital and provides telephone appointments for staff at smaller sites. Occupational Health will tell the manager only what is needed to plan duties, such as "can return to full duties with no lifting over 10 kg for 6 weeks", and not the underlying condition.

Q3. What is a fitness-for-work assessment and when is it used?

A fitness-for-work assessment is a structured review by an occupational physician or a suitably qualified clinician, arranged and paid for by the network. It is used when there is a genuine safety concern, after an extended absence, or where a staff member asks for one to support a return-to-work plan. Staff are given written notice of at least 5 working days before an assessment, are told what questions will be asked, and may bring a support person.

Q4. How long does the network keep medical certificates?

Medical certificates supporting personal leave are kept with leave records for the period required by employment record-keeping law, currently 7 years after the leave is taken. Certificates are scanned into the restricted leave record and the paper copy is destroyed within 30 days of scanning. Certificates must not be emailed to a general team inbox or stored in a ward folder.

Q5. What support is available for mental health and wellbeing?

All staff have access to the confidential Employee Assistance Program, with up to six free sessions per issue each year. The Lomandra Wellness Centre offers quiet rooms and drop-in sessions. Staff in mental health services, including the Tallowood Creek Mental Health Service and the Lignum Park Youth Mental Health Hub, also receive regular clinical supervision. Each year the network marks World Mental Health Day on 10 October 2026 and holds the Mental Health Week Community Walk in the same week; registrations close 14 days before the walk. Taking part is voluntary and does not involve disclosing anything about yourself.

---

PART B: IMMUNISATION

Q6. Which vaccinations are required?

Requirements depend on the risk category of the role. Category A roles, which involve direct patient or resident contact, require evidence of protection against a defined list of vaccine-preventable diseases before the start date. Category B and C roles have reduced requirements. The Infection Prevention Coordinator at each acute site maintains the current list, which is reviewed every 12 months.

Q7. When is the annual influenza vaccine due?

Influenza vaccination is offered free to all staff and volunteers through the Winter Flu Vaccination Drive. For the 2026 season, clinics open on 13 April 2026 and run for 8 weeks. Staff in aged care and other mandated settings must provide evidence of vaccination by 1 June 2026, or within 14 days of starting if they join after that date. Clinics run at Redgum Point Hospital, Wattlebird Ridge District Hospital and the community health centres, and mobile clinics visit Brolga Flat Lodge and the other residences.

Q8. What happens if a staff member cannot be vaccinated for medical reasons?

A medical exemption may be granted where a treating practitioner certifies a recognised contraindication. Exemption requests go directly to Occupational Health, not to the manager. If an exemption is granted, the manager is told only that the staff member has an approved exemption and, where needed, what protective measures apply. Exemptions are reviewed within 12 months or when the clinical guidance changes.

---

PART C: DISABILITY AND REASONABLE ADJUSTMENTS

Q9. What is a reasonable adjustment?

A reasonable adjustment is a change to the way work is done, the workplace or the equipment, which allows a person with disability to perform their role on an equal footing. Common examples across health services include adjustable workstations, screen-reading software, captioning on recorded training, modified rosters, a quieter work area, flexible break times and written rather than verbal handovers. Staff with a disability can request reasonable adjustments at any time, including during recruitment, at induction or later in their employment.

Q10. How is an adjustment requested?

Staff can complete the adjustment request form on the intranet, speak with their manager, or contact People and Culture directly through careers@kestrelplainshealth.example during recruitment, or the People and Culture adviser for their site after commencement. The network aims to respond to every request within 10 working days and to have agreed adjustments in place within 30 days. Requests that need building works or specialist equipment may take longer, and staff are kept informed of progress at least every 2 weeks.

Q11. Does the staff member have to provide medical evidence?

Not always. For many simple adjustments a conversation is enough. Where the adjustment is costly or significantly changes the role, the network may ask for information from a treating practitioner about functional needs. The network does not ask for a full medical history, and the information requested is limited to what is needed to design the adjustment.

Q12. How does the network improve accessibility more generally?

The Disability Inclusion Advisory Committee advises the executive on access, recruitment and inclusion. Each year the network holds Disability Access Audit Month, during which every site's buildings, signage, websites and forms are checked against the access plan, and findings are reported to the Board Audit and Risk Committee within 3 months. The network also marks International Day of People with Disability on 3 December 2026. All staff are encouraged to complete the online access awareness module, which is offered alongside Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials during induction.

---

PART D: FAITH, CULTURE AND OBSERVANCE

Q13. Can staff take time for prayer or religious observance during a shift?

Yes, where the needs of the service allow. Staff may use their break entitlements for prayer, and managers are asked to consider requests to adjust break times or rosters for daily, weekly or seasonal observance. Requests should be made as early as possible, ideally at least 4 weeks before the roster period begins. A request will only be declined where it cannot be accommodated without compromising safe staffing, and the reasons will be explained.

Q14. Are there prayer and reflection spaces?

Yes. Each acute site has a multi-faith room, and smaller sites have a designated quiet space. At Corella Downs Base Hospital the multi-faith room is next to the Paperbark Garden Lounge and includes washing facilities. The Pastoral Care Coordinator can provide information on local faith communities and on chaplaincy services for patients, residents and staff. The Faith and Pastoral Care Committee advises the network on facilities, catering and the observance calendar.

Q15. Can staff request leave for religious or cultural days?

Staff may request annual leave, time off in lieu or, where the enterprise agreement allows, a swap of a public holiday for another day of cultural or religious significance. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander staff are entitled to cultural and ceremonial leave as set out in the enterprise agreement. Staff do not have to explain the nature of a ceremony or observance in order to apply for leave, and requests are approved by the manager without being forwarded to other staff.

Q16. Does the network ask staff about their religion or cultural background?

Not as a condition of employment. The voluntary staff diversity survey includes optional questions about cultural background, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander status and religion. Answers are used only in aggregate, groups of fewer than 10 respondents are never reported, and every question includes a "prefer not to say" option. The Aboriginal Health Advisory Group and the Aboriginal Health Liaison Officer advise on how this information is used to improve cultural safety. Staff can also ask catering for dietary options for network events without stating a reason.

---

PART E: CRIMINAL RECORD AND WORKER SCREENING CHECKS

Q17. Which roles need a police check?

All employees, volunteers and students on placement in roles with direct patient, resident or client contact need a current national police check before they start. Roles that involve unsupervised contact with children, including those in Maternal and Child Health Outreach and the Youth Early Intervention Service, also need a working with children clearance where the law requires it. Roles in aged care and disability support may need additional screening under the relevant legislation.

Q18. How recent does the check need to be?

A police check must have been issued no more than 3 months before the start date. From 1 July 2026, checks for continuing staff in screened roles are renewed every 3 years, and People and Culture will send a reminder 60 days before the renewal is due. Staff whose renewal is not completed within 30 days after the due date may be moved temporarily to duties that do not require a check.

Q19. Does having a criminal record mean someone cannot work for the network?

No. A disclosable outcome on a police check does not automatically exclude a person from employment or volunteering. The network assesses each outcome against the inherent requirements of the specific role, considering the nature and seriousness of the offence, how long ago it occurred, the person's age at the time, whether it is relevant to the duties, and any evidence of rehabilitation. The applicant is always given the opportunity to provide information before a decision is made.

Q20. Who sees the result of a police check?

Results are viewed only by the screening officer in People and Culture and, where a disclosable outcome needs assessment, by a small panel that includes the Quality and Risk Manager or a nominee. Managers are told only whether a person has been cleared for the role. Check certificates are stored in a restricted file, separate from the personnel file, and are destroyed within 12 months after the decision unless the law requires a longer period.

Q21. What must staff do if they are charged with an offence while employed?

Staff in screened roles must tell People and Culture within 7 days if they are charged with or convicted of an offence that is relevant to their role, as set out in the screening policy. The network will then consider whether any interim change to duties is needed. A charge is not treated as a finding of guilt, and staff are entitled to have a support person or union representative present at any meeting about the matter.

Q22. Do volunteers and students go through the same process?

Yes, with the same safeguards. Volunteer screening is coordinated by the Volunteer Coordinator through volunteers@kestrelplainshealth.example, and student placement screening is coordinated with the education provider before the placement begins. Students must provide evidence of a current check at least 10 working days before their first shift.

---

PART F: UNION MEMBERSHIP AND WORKPLACE RELATIONS

Q23. Does the network have a view on whether staff join a union?

Staff are free to join, or not to join, a union. The network will not ask staff whether they are union members, and will not treat anyone differently because they are or are not a member. Union membership is never recorded in performance, rostering or recruitment records.

Q24. Can union dues be deducted from pay?

Yes, where a staff member asks for it. Payroll deduction is set up by the Payroll Officer on written authority from the staff member and can be cancelled at any time with 14 days' notice. The deduction record is visible only to the payroll team and is not shared with managers.

Q25. How does the network consult with unions?

The Union Consultative Committee meets every 2 months and is the main forum for consultation on rosters, restructures, workplace health and safety, and changes to policies such as this one. Union officials with a right of entry may visit sites in accordance with the law and are asked to sign in at reception. Workplace delegates are given reasonable paid time to attend training and represent members, as provided in the enterprise agreement.

Q26. Where can staff raise a workplace health and safety concern?

Concerns can be raised with a manager, a health and safety representative, or the Occupational Health and Safety Committee. Hazards and incidents should be logged in the incident reporting system within 24 hours. Staff working in community settings should also complete Occupational Violence Prevention within 3 months of starting and every 2 years after that.

---

PART G: FAMILY AND DOMESTIC VIOLENCE SUPPORT

Q27. What leave is available?

All employees, including casual employees, can access paid family and domestic violence leave in line with the National Employment Standards and the enterprise agreement. The leave can be used for activities such as attending court, relocating, attending appointments or arranging safety measures. Staff do not need to provide evidence to start the leave, and any evidence requested later is kept confidential and stored separately from the personnel file.

Q28. What other support is available?

Staff can request changes to their roster, work location, phone number or email display name, and can ask for their details to be removed from public staff lists and switchboard directories. Security staff at each site can provide escorts to car parks. Requests for these changes can be made confidentially through People and Culture or the Social Worker assigned to staff support at each acute site, without involving the line manager. A list of external support services is available on the intranet and at every reception desk.

---

PART H: HOW THE NETWORK HANDLES THIS INFORMATION

Q29. Who can access sensitive staff information?

Access is limited to the people who need it to provide the support or meet the legal obligation: Occupational Health for health information, the screening officer for police checks, Payroll for union deductions and People and Culture advisers for adjustment and leave records. Access to these restricted records is logged, and the logs are reviewed by the Health Information Manager every 6 months.

Q30. Can staff see the information held about them?

Yes. Staff can ask to see or correct the information the network holds about them. Requests can be made through records@kestrelplainshealth.example, and the network aims to respond within 30 days. Formal access requests under freedom of information legislation are handled by the Freedom of Information Officer through foi@kestrelplainshealth.example.

Q31. What should staff do if sensitive information is shared without permission?

Report it straight away to the Privacy Officer at privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example. Suspected privacy breaches must be reported within 24 hours of being identified, and the Privacy Officer will assess the matter within 30 days. If the breach involves a system, such as a misdirected email or an incorrect access setting, also log a request with the service desk at servicedesk@kestrelplainshealth.example. The service desk recently closed ticket SD-4471820, which removed an old shared folder of scanned leave forms from a general drive; the folder had been created before this policy took effect.

Q32. Do staff need training on this policy?

All staff complete Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials (TRN-1210) at induction and every 2 years. Managers also complete a short module on handling disclosures, adjustment requests and screening outcomes within 3 months of appointment. Training is delivered online and in person at the Mulga Education Centre.

---

PART I: CONTACTS

General enquiries: enquiries@kestrelplainshealth.example or (03) 7010 2000
Privacy questions and breach reports: privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example
Feedback on this document: feedback@kestrelplainshealth.example
IT access and records system issues: servicedesk@kestrelplainshealth.example
Volunteer screening: volunteers@kestrelplainshealth.example
Recruitment and pre-employment adjustments: careers@kestrelplainshealth.example

Site reception numbers for local contacts:
- Corella Downs Base Hospital: (03) 5550 1101
- Redgum Point Hospital: (03) 5550 1102
- Wattlebird Ridge District Hospital: (03) 5550 1103
- Tallowood Creek Mental Health Service: (03) 5550 1114
- Lignum Park Youth Mental Health Hub: (03) 5550 1116

Staff networks and advisory groups that welcome new members include the Pride Staff Network, the Women in Health Leadership Network and the Mental Health Lived Experience Advisory Group. Joining a network is voluntary and does not involve disclosing anything about yourself. Network events such as the Pride in Health Morning Tea and the Carers Recognition Breakfast are open to all staff.

---

DOCUMENT CONTROL

Version 3.0. Consolidates the former health and fitness for work, immunisation, reasonable adjustment, religious observance, worker screening and family violence fact sheets.

Chapter Four

Thursday

The bell for period three rang while Teddy was still fighting the combination on her locker outside B Block. Someone had jammed a muesli bar wrapper into the dial again. She kicked the door, which did nothing, then kicked it a second time, which did something. It swung open on a slump of textbooks and the envelope she had been carrying around since the weekend.

The envelope had a crest in one corner. Her father's name was typed beneath it, LASZLO VARGA, in the kind of capitals that made it look like a shipping label. Inside, on paper so thin she could see her own fingers through it, was the new visiting schedule. Her dad had been inside Warrigal Correctional Centre for fourteen months now. Nobody at Bellbird Creek High knew that. Not her year adviser, not the girls she ate lunch with under the jacarandas, not the careers teacher who kept asking whether her parents would be coming to the subject selection evening. When anyone asked, she said he was working out west. It was nearly true. Warrigal was west. You could see the wheat silos from the car park.

The next visit fell on the long weekend after Anzac Day. That meant two trains out of Central Station and then the coach, and every carriage would be packed with families heading somewhere with a beach. Teddy had worked it out on the back of her chemistry book: three hours each way for forty minutes on a moulded plastic chair. During those forty minutes her father would ask about her marks and she would ask about the welding course he was doing through the education unit on the inside. They would both pretend the officer by the vending machine wasn't listening.

Last time he had held her hand across the table until a guard tapped the glass. He had cried when she left, quickly, the way he used to sneeze, as if it embarrassed him.

She shoved the envelope back under her maths textbook and ran.

English Advanced was in Room B12. The window had been painted shut sometime in the nineties, and the poster of the Romantic poets had faded until they all looked equally seasick. The class was halfway through a poem about walls. Of course it was. Their teacher read the last stanza aloud in his voice for Important Lines and asked what the speaker was really locked out of.

Teddy looked at the page. The words sat there, black and patient, and she felt the room tilt very slightly, the way it did at Warrigal when the second door closed behind you before the first one opened.

"Anyone?" he said.

She put her hand up before she could stop herself.

"Maybe he isn't locked out," Teddy said. "Maybe he's the one inside, and he's just being polite about it."

The room went quiet in a way she couldn't read. Then the teacher smiled, wrote *polite* on the whiteboard and underlined it twice. Afterwards she couldn't stop seeing it there, white on white, until the bell went again.

text:
ARDBROOK PRIVATE BANK
Operations Risk | Post-Incident Review Report

Incident reference: INC-0048213
Conduct and privacy case: OPS-CASE-20417
Site: Kingsmead Operations Centre, Adelaide
Prepared by: Harriet Lindqvist, Operations Risk
Classification: Internal – Restricted. Do not forward outside the distribution list in Appendix C.

1. Executive summary

This report reviews how an unprotected working spreadsheet ("KYC_refresh_tracker_v3.xlsx") was created and shared in the Client Onboarding team at the Kingsmead Operations Centre. The team built the file to chase overdue identity re-verifications for 214 private banking clients. It also held full passport numbers, full Medicare card numbers, client callback numbers and free-text vulnerability notes. None of these were needed. The file sat on a shared drive that every operations user could read for nine working days. A Payments Exceptions analyst then noticed it and logged INC-0048213.

We found no evidence that the file left the bank. Access logs show 31 internal accounts opened it, and 27 of them belonged to people with no business need. The review panel met on 12 March 2026 and again on 19 March 2026 to agree the findings below.

Overall rating: Significant (control design failure, no confirmed external disclosure).

2. Background

Under the bank's periodic review standard, private clients whose identity documents are close to expiry must be re-verified before the document lapses. In late January, Compliance sent Onboarding a backlog list of clients due for re-verification. The Onboarding team lead, Mei-Lin Tran (network login mltran_ops), asked two staff to build a tracker so that callers could work through the list.

The tracker was built from a full extract of the client identity table. It should have used the masked view that the Head of Client Onboarding approved in 2024. The masked view shows only the last four characters of each document number and leaves out health and vulnerability notes completely.

3. Sequence of events (summary)

- Week 1, Monday: the extract is run and pasted into the tracker. The file is saved to the general Operations share instead of the restricted Onboarding folder.
- Week 1, Wednesday to Week 2, Thursday: callers update the file daily. Three further copies ("v1", "v2", "v3") are made in the same location.
- Week 2, Friday, 16:40: Tomasz Wierzbicki (login tomw.kms) opens the share to look for a payments template, sees the file and raises INC-0048213.
- Week 2, Friday, 17:25: IT removes access to all four copies. The Privacy Officer is notified and opens OPS-CASE-20417.

4. Findings

F1. Over-collection of identity numbers.
The tracker held full document numbers for every client row. For example, the row for client Gerald Ashworth showed passport PY2036043, recorded as expiring 14 August 2026, and Medicare card 5627 12797 1. Ashworth had already booked a branch re-verification appointment for 27 March 2026. His row therefore did not need to appear on the call list at all.

F2. Vulnerability and health notes copied into free text.
The extract included the "client care notes" column, which callers can normally see only on screen within the CRM. One row states that client Fatima Al-Sayegh is having chemotherapy on Wednesdays and asked for calls only after 2 pm. Her row also held her passport number, Medicare number and personal mobile (see Appendix A). Anyone with read access to the share could see these notes.

F3. Access control on the Operations share.
The general Operations share is open to every operations account, including contractors and overnight staff. Log review shows that the only analyst on the overnight sanctions-screening roster opened the file 14 times. When interviewed, the analyst said the file appeared at the top of the "recent files" list and was opened by mistake. Nothing indicates misuse, but the pattern shows the share gave no protection at all.

F4. Detection relied on chance.
Data loss prevention rules did not flag the file, because they scan outbound email and not internal shares. The file was found only because Wierzbicki noticed it and reported it at once. Tomasz, who is the union delegate for the operations floor, also told the panel that staff need to hear clearly that callers who used the tracker in good faith will not be disciplined. The panel accepted that point.

5. Contributing factors

The tracker was built by Daniel Okonkwo-Reid together with the one contractor seconded from Perth to the onboarding pod. The contractor started on 19 January 2026 and had not yet completed the bank's data handling induction. Daniel returned to work on 2 February 2026 and was working reduced hours during the week the file was built.

Supervision was also thin. The Payments Exceptions team leader, who normally co-signs bulk extracts with Onboarding, was on reduced hours while recovering from a hip replacement. No delegate had been named for extract approvals. Mei-Lin approved the extract request by message without seeing which columns it included.

The panel considers these to be system weaknesses rather than individual failings. The extract tool lets any team lead export unmasked columns, and nothing prompts the user before a file is saved to an open share.

6. Recommendations

R1. Restrict the client identity extract so that only the masked view can be exported without second approval from the Head of Operations Risk. Owner: MLT. Due: end of quarter.
R2. Add internal share scanning to the DLP rule set, covering passport, Medicare and card number patterns. Owner: IT Security.
R3. Name a standing delegate for extract approvals whenever a co-signer is on leave or reduced hours. Owner: Operations Management.
R4. Complete data handling induction before any contractor receives Onboarding access. Owner: People and Culture.
R5. Contact the affected clients where full document numbers or care notes were exposed. Offer document replacement support where clients ask for it. Owner: Privacy Officer.

Appendix A – Excerpt of exposed rows (as recovered)

The excerpt below was copied from the recovered "v3" file. Line wrapping has been kept as it appeared in the original export.

Row 042 | ASHWORTH, Gerald | Passport PY2036043 | Medicare 5627 12797 1 | Status: branch appt booked
Row 117 | AL-SAYEGH, Fatima | Passport WK7436518 exp 30 April 2026 | Medicare 3945 76974 8 | Callback (client preference): 0491 572
028, after 2 pm only. See care note.

All other rows follow the same layout. The full file is held by the Privacy Officer under OPS-CASE-20417 and is not attached to this report.

Appendix B – Extract from staff statement (D. Okonkwo-Reid)

"I had come back that week after a fortnight off with glandular fever and was still on half days, so I took the quickest route. I ran the full extract, pasted it in and meant to delete the extra columns afterwards. I saved it to the Operations share because the Onboarding folder kept timing out. I didn't go back to it before the callers started using it. I understand now that the masked view was the right source."

Statement taken by H. Lindqvist in the presence of T. Wierzbicki, at Daniel's request.

Appendix C – Distribution

Head of Operations Risk; Head of Client Onboarding; Privacy Officer; Review panel members (meetings of 12 March 2026 and 19 March 2026).

H. Lindqvist
Operations Risk, Kingsmead Operations Centre

text:
Staff Information: Health, Disability, Faith, Criminal Record Checks and Union Matters at Work
Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network
Policy reference: 40271936 | Supersedes form F-2208 | Owner: Director of Clinical Governance

This FAQ explains how KPCN handles sensitive matters that staff, volunteers and students may raise at work. It describes general policy only. It applies at every campus, including Corella Downs Base Hospital, Redgum Point Hospital and our community health centres.

1. Do I have to tell my manager about a health condition?
No. You only need to tell us about a condition if it affects your ability to work safely or if you want support. Anything you disclose goes to the people who need it to arrange adjustments. It is not placed on your general personnel file. The Nurse Unit Manager or line manager will usually involve Occupational Health. They will not ask for a diagnosis unless it is clinically necessary.

2. How do I request a workplace adjustment for a disability?
Staff with a disability can request reasonable adjustments at any stage of employment. Examples include changed rosters, assistive technology, an accessible workstation or a hearing loop in meeting rooms. Send requests to careers@kestrelplainshealth.example during recruitment, or to your manager once employed. The Disability Inclusion Advisory Committee reviews access across the network. Each year it runs Disability Access Audit Month, timed to finish near International Day of People with Disability on 3 December 2026.

3. Can I take time for religious observance?
Yes. Managers will try to accommodate prayer times, fasting periods and holy days where rosters allow. Requests should normally be made at least 4 weeks ahead. Multi-faith rooms are available at the larger campuses. The Pastoral Care Coordinator and the Faith and Pastoral Care Committee can advise on dietary and cultural needs for staff events.

4. Why does the network require police checks?
All roles involving patient, resident or client contact require a national police check before the start date. Many roles also require a Working with Children Check. A criminal record does not automatically exclude an applicant. Each result is assessed against the inherent requirements of the role. Checks are renewed every 3 years. Results are held by People and Culture and are not shared with the hiring panel beyond the outcome.

5. Am I allowed to join a union or attend union meetings?
Yes. Union membership is a matter for each employee, and no one may be treated differently for joining or not joining. Workplace delegates may hold meetings in break times. The Union Consultative Committee meets with management on proposed changes to rosters and enterprise agreements.

6. Where can I get confidential support?
The Employee Assistance Program is free and confidential. Peer support is also offered during the Mental Health Week Community Walk and through the Pride Staff Network. Staff can also complete TRN-1210 Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials to understand how disclosures are protected.

7. Who do I contact with a privacy concern?
Contact the Privacy Officer at privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example or call (03) 7010 2000. Complaints are acknowledged within 5 business days.

The note is recorded here only so that the declaration is filed correctly and not re-opened by the site.

TK asked that both declarations be stored in the restricted screening folder and not in the general personnel file.

This is because the position number on the request did not match the cost centre. AD expects this to be fixed well before Darcy's start date of 6 April 2026. Because of the Easter long weekend, the sign-in letter will be posted rather than handed over on site.

- Graduate Nurse Welcome Week planning is under way. Onboarding packs must be finalised two weeks beforehand.

THE WINTER COUNT
A novel

Chapter Seven
Thursday

The rain came in off the plateau the way it always did at Cauldron Bluff, sideways and without apology. Margit Fennow had the kettle on before the generator finished coughing. By the time the radio crackled she had already decided that the track crew would not be going up to Wrecker's Saddle today, whatever the Commission's work plan said.

"Base, this is Two," said the radio. It was Elias Crane, and he sounded like a man standing in a creek.

"Go ahead, Two."

"Footbridge at the second crossing's gone. Clean gone. I'll walk back the long way round."

She wrote the time in the log and did not ask whether he would make it down before dark. Nobody at the Highland Reserves Commission asked Elias anything they did not have to. Everyone knew he had spent four winters in the gaol at Kelpie Ferry for setting fire to his father's boatshed, and everyone knew he still drove two hours into town every Thursday to sign the book at the corrections office. That was why the job had come to him at all. Nobody else wanted the western huts, and a man on a supervision order takes what he is given.

Margit had never minded him. He kept the hut logs neater than anyone, and he was the only ranger who scraped the boot-wash station without being told. Once, the previous autumn, he had driven her all the way down to Hobart for the Anzac Day dawn service. Her grandfather's name was on the cenotaph there, and her own car had thrown a belt at the turn-off. He had stood at the back of the crowd with his hands in his pockets. Afterwards he said only that it was colder than the plateau, which was not true.

The light went the colour of pewter. At four o'clock she radioed again and got static. At half past, she put on her coat.

She found him at the top of the old pack track, sitting on the trig cairn with his boots off, pouring water out of them like a man emptying a teapot.

"You'll lose your toes," she said.

"Not today." Elias looked out past her, towards where Lake St Clair would be if the cloud ever lifted. "They want me in town early tomorrow. New officer. Wants to see the hut rosters, see if I'm where I say I am."

"You are where you say you are."

"That's never been the question with them." He laced the wet boots back up, slowly, and stood. "Come on. Kettle'll have boiled dry."

They walked down together in the last of the light, and neither of them said anything more about it, which was the closest thing to kindness the plateau allowed.

From The Winter Count, Chapter Seven. All characters and places in this novel are invented, apart from well-known public landmarks.
