Staff Wellbeing, Inclusion and Pre-Employment Checks: Frequently Asked Questions

Applies to: all employees, students on placement and volunteers of Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network (KPCN)
Owner: People and Culture, with input from the Clinical Governance Committee
Review cycle: every 2 years, or sooner if legislation changes

1. Do I have to tell my manager about a health condition?

No. Staff do not have to disclose a medical condition unless it affects their ability to do their role safely. If you think a condition may affect safe work, speak with your Nurse Unit Manager or line manager. Any health information you share is kept on a confidential file separate from your general personnel record. Only people who need it to arrange support can see it.

2. How do I ask for a reasonable adjustment?

Staff with a disability or long-term condition can ask for reasonable adjustments at any time, including before they start. Examples include modified rosters, accessible workstations, assistive software and changes to how meetings are run. Requests are normally answered within 10 working days. The Disability Inclusion Advisory Committee reviews the adjustment process each year. Site accessibility is checked during Disability Access Audit Month.

3. Can I take time for prayer or religious observance?

Yes. Quiet rooms are available on each acute campus, including Corella Downs Base Hospital and Redgum Point Hospital. Leave or roster swaps for religious festivals should be requested at least 4 weeks ahead where possible. The Pastoral Care Coordinator can advise on multi-faith resources. The Faith and Pastoral Care Committee oversees chaplaincy and pastoral services for patients and staff.

4. Why does the network ask for a police check?

All roles that involve patient, resident or client contact need a current national police check before the start date. These checks are renewed every 3 years. Aged-care and youth roles may also need additional screening required by law. A disclosed record does not automatically rule anyone out. Each disclosure is assessed against the inherent requirements of the role, and results are destroyed after the retention period set by the records schedule. Questions about the process can be sent to careers@kestrelplainshealth.example.

5. Does the network record union membership?

No. Staff are free to join, or not join, a union. Membership is never recorded on personnel files. Payroll deductions for union fees are optional and handled only on the staff member's written request. Workplace change that affects employment conditions is discussed through the Union Consultative Committee.

6. What mental health support is available?

The Employee Assistance Program offers confidential counselling, with 6 free sessions per year. Staff and their household can also join community events such as the Mental Health Week Community Walk, held near World Mental Health Day (10 October 2026).

7. How is my information protected?

All staff complete Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials (TRN-1210) within 3 months of starting. Concerns about how personal or health information is handled can go to the Privacy Officer at privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example or through the main line on (03) 7010 2000. Complaints are acknowledged within 5 working days.

text:
Quenda Rise Engineering Partners
Internal Audit Report: Field Instrument Calibration and Asset Register Controls
Report reference: QRA-2026-07
Issued: 14 August 2026
Prepared by: Internal Audit Lead, for the Audit and Risk Committee
Distribution: Managing Director, Chief Operating Officer, Group Asset Manager, Quality Systems Manager

1. Purpose and scope

This report sets out the results of the scheduled audit of field instrument calibration and the fixed asset register at Quenda Rise Engineering Partners. The audit was approved by the Audit and Risk Committee at its meeting of 19 May 2026. Fieldwork ran over six weeks across the three operating sites: the Marri Terrace head office, the Tuart Lane Laboratory and the Jarrahvale Field Depot.

The audit covered:

- survey, geotechnical and structural monitoring instruments with a purchase value above $2,000;
- calibration certificates issued or renewed in the twelve months to 30 June 2026;
- the transfer of equipment between sites and project teams;
- supplier invoices charged to the calibration and maintenance cost centres.

Staff records, payroll and individual performance were outside scope. No interviews were recorded against named individuals. Observations are attributed to roles and sites only.

2. Summary of findings

Overall rating: Needs improvement.

The asset register is broadly complete and the calibration schedule is understood at all three sites. However, the audit found gaps in how equipment moves between projects, a backlog of certificates that were not uploaded to the register, and a small number of invoices coded to the wrong cost centre. None of the findings indicate loss of equipment. Two findings carry a moderate risk rating because instruments used on client deliverables could not be shown to be in calibration on the date of use.

| No. | Finding | Rating | Owner (role) |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Calibration certificates not attached to register entries | Moderate | Quality Systems Manager |
| F2 | Equipment transfers between sites not logged within 5 working days | Moderate | Depot Supervisor |
| F3 | Invoices coded to the wrong cost centre | Low | Finance Business Partner |
| F4 | Retired assets still shown as active | Low | Group Asset Manager |

3. Detailed findings

3.1 F1: Certificates not attached to the register

A sample of 60 instruments was drawn from the register. For 11 of them the calibration certificate existed on the shared drive but had not been attached to the register entry, so the register showed the instrument as overdue. The issue was concentrated at the Tuart Lane Laboratory, where certificates are scanned in Sample Prep Room 2 and uploaded in batches.

Examples from the sample:

- Total station QRE-SV-04471: certificate dated within the cycle, not attached.
- Vibrating wire readout unit QRE-GT-01186: certificate held by the external laboratory, copy not requested.
- Digital level QRE-SV-04502: certificate attached to a retired sister unit in error.

The calibration procedure requires certificates to be uploaded within 10 working days of receipt. That requirement is not being met at the laboratory. The current register build, 4.12.3, supports bulk upload, but the feature has not been switched on.

Recommendation: Enable bulk upload in the register and set a monthly reconciliation between the shared drive and the register. Target date: 30 September 2026, to be reported at the following committee meeting.

3.2 F2: Transfers between sites

Instruments regularly move from the Jarrahvale Field Depot to project sites and back. The transfer form QR-F-112 is in use, but in 9 of 24 transfers tested the form was completed more than 5 working days after the move. In three cases the register still showed the instrument at the depot while it was in use on a client project.

The depot's equipment cage in Workshop Building B has no sign-out terminal. Transfers are recorded on paper and keyed in later by the Depot Administration Officer role, which is a part-time position.

Recommendation: Install a sign-out tablet at the cage, and make the register the single point of record for location. A procurement request has been raised as CASE-7731.

3.3 F3: Cost centre coding

Calibration and repair costs should be charged to cost centre CC-3120 (Instrument Calibration) or CC-3125 (Field Equipment Maintenance). Four invoices from the past financial year had been charged to CC-4410 (Project Consumables) instead:

| Invoice | Supplier category | Amount (ex GST) | Coded to | Should be |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| INV-QR-20817 | Calibration laboratory | $3,940.00 | CC-4410 | CC-3120 |
| INV-QR-20944 | Instrument repairer | $1,275.50 | CC-4410 | CC-3125 |
| INV-QR-21003 | Calibration laboratory | $2,610.00 | CC-4410 | CC-3120 |
| INV-QR-21152 | Freight and courier | $486.20 | CC-4410 | CC-3125 |

The total misallocation is $8,311.70. It does not change the annual result but it understates the calibration budget line, which is used to set next year's allocation.

Recommendation: Journal the four invoices to the correct cost centres before the end of the first quarter, and add a coding hint to the purchase order template for calibration suppliers.

3.4 F4: Retired assets

Seven instruments flagged for disposal in the previous year still appear as active. One of them, data logger QRE-MN-00893, was returned to the manufacturer under warranty and replaced. The replacement unit was registered correctly, so the logger now appears twice in the location report.

Recommendation: The Group Asset Manager to run a disposal review each quarter and close entries within 30 days of disposal.

4. Management response

Management accepts all four findings. Actions will be tracked in the corrective action register under CASE-7738, and a progress update will be tabled at the committee meeting of 17 November 2026. The Quality Systems Manager will report completion of F1 and F2 within 3 months of this report.

5. Contacts

Questions about this report should go to the internal audit mailbox, internal.audit@quendarise.example. Questions about the asset register go to assets@quendarise.example. Suppliers with invoice queries can call the accounts line on 1800 975 710 during business hours.

Appendix A: Sampling method

The register held 412 active instruments at the start of fieldwork. A stratified sample of 60 was drawn: 30 from the Jarrahvale Field Depot, 20 from the Tuart Lane Laboratory and 10 from the Marri Terrace head office. Selection used the register's random-sample report. Each sampled item was physically sighted, its tag checked against the register and its current certificate located.

Appendix B: Rooms and locations visited

- Marri Terrace head office: Level 3 Equipment Store, Meeting Room Banksia
- Tuart Lane Laboratory: Sample Prep Room 2, Calibration Bay 1
- Jarrahvale Field Depot: Workshop Building B, equipment cage and vehicle bay

Appendix C: Related documents

- Calibration and Verification Procedure, QP-CAL-004 rev 6
- Asset Management Policy, QP-AST-001 rev 3
- Prior audit report QRA-2025-04, closed at the meeting of 10 February 2026

End of report.

Dear Asset Manager,

**Re: Structural condition assessment of the Northern Storage Reservoir roof and access arrangements for the June inspection window**

Thank you for the instruction issued under the panel arrangement and confirmed through the client portal under ticket HD-58213. This letter sets out the proposed scope, programme and access requirements for the structural condition assessment of the reservoir roof, its supporting columns and the adjoining Pump Station Control Building at the Northern Storage site. It also confirms the arrangements agreed in principle at the coordination meeting held in Meeting Room 4B on 7 May 2026.

**1. Scope of the assessment**

The assessment will cover the following elements:

(a) the steel roof trusses, purlins and sheeting over the full reservoir footprint, including the access hatches and ventilation cowls;
(b) the reinforced concrete perimeter wall from the crest down to the top of the internal ladder landing;
(c) the internal column grid, including visible base connections where water levels permit;
(d) the roof plant platform and handrailing adjacent to the Valve House No. 2; and
(e) the external stair tower linking the reservoir roof to the Pump Station Control Building.

The work will be carried out under our standard structural inspection procedure, QP-STR-011, and the findings will be recorded against your asset register using the tags already held in your maintenance system. Where a tag cannot be located on site, our team will log the element against the nearest tagged asset and flag it in the report for your records group to resolve.

**2. Programme**

We propose to mobilise on 8 June 2026, the Monday following the Western Australia Day long weekend (1 June 2026 falls on the preceding Monday and site access is unavailable that day). The inspection is expected to take 72 hours of on-roof work, spread across three consecutive day shifts. A draft report will be issued within 15 business days of demobilisation, and the final report within 10 business days of receiving your consolidated comments.

Please note the following programme constraints:

- the reservoir must be drawn down to no more than 40 per cent of operating level at least 24 hours before mobilisation, so that the column bases are visible from the internal ladder landing;
- isolation of the roof ventilation fans must be confirmed in writing no later than 48 hours before the first shift; and
- if wind speeds at the site exceed the limit set out in our work method statement, roof work will be suspended and the programme extended day for day.

Should the drawdown not be achievable in June, the next suitable window identified by your operations team begins on 3 August 2026 and would add approximately 8 weeks to the overall reporting timeline.

**3. Site access and induction**

All personnel attending site will complete your contractor induction before mobilisation. Our understanding is that induction sessions are held in the Training Room 1 of the Operations Centre at Northern Storage Reservoir, and that bookings are made through your contractor management mailbox, contractors@halvorsenbasin.example. Inductions remain valid for 12 months, and personnel whose induction has lapsed will be re-inducted before entering the operational area.

Each shift will be supervised by our Site Supervisor, who will hold the daily permit to work and attend the pre-start briefing with your Operations Coordinator. A rescue plan for work at height and in the vicinity of the open reservoir will be submitted with the work method statement at least 10 business days before mobilisation.

Our crew on this project includes subcontracted rope-access technicians, several of whom work most comfortably in Vietnamese. To support clear communication on site, the key access requirements will be issued to all crews in English and Vietnamese. The Vietnamese text to be included in the site briefing pack is reproduced below for your review:

> Thông báo dành cho các đội thầu phụ: Từ ngày 8 tháng 6 năm 2026, khu vực mái bể chứa phía Bắc sẽ được mở cho công tác kiểm tra kết cấu trong 72 giờ làm việc, chia thành ba ca ban ngày liên tiếp. Tất cả nhân viên phải hoàn thành buổi hướng dẫn an toàn của chủ đầu tư trước khi vào công trường, đăng ký tại cổng an ninh mỗi sáng và mang đầy đủ đồ bảo hộ cá nhân. Không ai được lên mái khi chưa có giấy phép làm việc trong ngày do Giám sát Công trường ký. Nếu tốc độ gió vượt quá giới hạn cho phép, công việc trên mái sẽ tạm dừng. Mọi thắc mắc xin gửi về hộp thư dự án projects@coralbankeng.example và ghi rõ số tham chiếu CSC-2026-0417.

We would be grateful if your Communications team could confirm whether this translation may be posted on the site noticeboard alongside your standard safety signage.

**4. Deliverables**

The deliverables for this engagement are:

1. a work method statement and rescue plan, issued at least 10 business days before mobilisation;
2. a daily site record, issued by close of business at the end of each shift;
3. a draft condition assessment report, including a defect schedule, photographic record and priority ratings for each element;
4. a final report incorporating your comments; and
5. a presentation of findings to your Asset Planning Committee, if requested, at a meeting to be scheduled within 30 days of the final report.

Defects rated as requiring immediate attention will be reported verbally to your Operations Coordinator on the day they are identified and confirmed in writing within 24 hours, without waiting for the draft report.

**5. Commercial matters**

The fee for this engagement remains as set out in our proposal dated 22 April 2026. Any additional site days arising from weather, delayed drawdown or access restrictions will be charged at the panel day rate, subject to your prior written approval. Invoices will quote purchase order PO-772104 and will be issued to accounts@halvorsenbasin.example at the end of each month.

**6. Records and correspondence**

All correspondence relating to this engagement should quote our reference CSC-2026-0417 and your ticket HD-58213. Project correspondence may be sent to projects@coralbankeng.example; requests for copies of superseded drawings should be directed to records@coralbankeng.example. Our document control register is retained for 7 years from completion of the engagement in accordance with our quality management system.

We note that our office will be closed for the Christmas Day and New Year period from 25 December 2026, and we would ask that any comments on the final report be returned before 11 December 2026 to allow close-out within the current calendar year.

**7. Next steps**

To keep the June window available, we would appreciate your written confirmation of the following within 10 business days of the date of this letter:

- acceptance of the scope set out in section 1;
- confirmation that the reservoir drawdown can be achieved at least 24 hours before 8 June 2026;
- the names of the induction session times available in the week of 1 June 2026 at the Operations Centre; and
- approval to post the bilingual briefing notice on site.

A follow-up coordination meeting has been pencilled in for 28 May 2026 in Meeting Room 4B at our East Perth office, with a video link available for your operations team.

Thank you for the opportunity to continue supporting your reservoir renewal programme. Please do not hesitate to contact the project team through the mailbox above should you require any clarification.

Yours faithfully,

Project Director, Water Infrastructure

Rātā Commons Housing Co-operative
Privacy Incident Review: Misdirected Membership Application Pack
Helpdesk reference: HD-20417
Prepared by: Sione Fifita, Privacy and Compliance Lead
Distribution: Board Risk and Audit Committee; Tenancy Services Manager

1. Summary

A membership application pack for a household moving into a two-bedroom unit at Pōhutukawa Court was emailed to the wrong external address. The recipient was a private individual with a similar email address. They deleted the message and confirmed this in writing within a day. This report sets out what was disclosed, why it happened and what we will change.

2. Background

The applicant, Ariel Mizrahi-Tane, recently returned to Aotearoa after several years working in Australia and the United Kingdom. Her pack was assembled by Hemi Paraone, Tenancy Officer, and sent from a shared tablet at the front desk. The address was chosen from the autocomplete list. No second check was done before sending.

3. Information disclosed

The pack contained the following:

- Ariel's Australian tax file number, 820 602 907, included on a former employer's payment summary.
- Her partner's UK National Insurance number, QQ 26 30 45 D, from a reference letter.
- Bank details for the bond refund: 999-009 64191027.
- A link to Ariel's design portfolio, https://portfolio.example/ariel-mt, given as her work history.
- Her answers to the household needs form. These record that Ariel keeps Shabbat and asked that no inspection or working bee be booked from Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall. Her partner stated on the same form that he has no religious affiliation.

By comparison, co-op policy already pauses routine inspections over Easter and Matariki for all units. That scheduling rule says nothing about any member.

4. Findings

4.1 Autocomplete on the shared tablet was the direct cause. Hemi acted in good faith and reported the error himself within ten minutes.

4.2 We do not need a tax file number or a National Insurance number for membership. These documents were accepted "for completeness", which goes against our own collection guidance.

4.3 The household needs form asks an open question about "anything we should know". Faith-related scheduling needs are therefore recorded in free text. They should sit in a restricted field that is visible only to the tenancy team.

4.4 Ariel Mizrahi-Tane was told the same day. She has asked that her bank details be replaced and that the old ones be removed from the file.

5. Recommendations

R1. Turn off autocomplete on front-desk devices.
R2. Redact overseas tax and social-security numbers when documents are received.
R3. Move scheduling needs to a restricted field and refer the form wording to the Member Wellbeing and Inclusion Committee.
R4. Run a refresher session for tenancy staff before the next intake.

Appendix A: Timeline

Tue 14:52, pack sent.
Tue 15:01, Hemi reports the error to the Tenancy Services Manager.
Wed 09:30, recipient confirms deletion.
Wed 11:15, applicant informed by phone.

Appendix B: Contact

Questions about this review can go to the front desk on (03) 7010 6519, quoting HD-20417.

Sione Fifita
Privacy and Compliance Lead

The vendor will apply a database upgrade to the scheduling platform, taking it from version 4.12.2 to 4.13.0 (build 30817). We moved this work away from the King's Birthday (Victoria) long weekend (8 June 2026) so that the after-hours on-call roster is not stretched.

Bellbird Valley Water | Operational Technology Service Desk
Ticket export (full thread)

Ticket number: OTS-418702
Title: Alarm notifications not reaching on-call handset after alarm dispatch patch, Gannet Hill WTP
Status: Resolved, pending CAB review
Priority: P2 (operational impact, manual workaround in place)
Category: Operational Technology > SCADA > Alarm Dispatch
Site: Gannet Hill Water Treatment Plant
Location: Clearwell Control Building, Control Room 2
Asset: BVW-AS-30417 (alarm dispatch server, virtual)
Related change: CHG-55821
Related project: CAP-TEL-26 (Telemetry Renewal Stage 2)
Requested by: Treatment Plant Operator (night shift roster)
Assigned group: OT Systems
Assigned to: OT Systems Engineer (on-call)
Notify: otsupport@bellbirdvalleywater.example; duty.manager@bellbirdvalleywater.example
Opened: Mon 05:52
Resolved: Tue 16:20

---------------------------------------------------------------------
Description (entered by requester)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
During the overnight shift at Gannet Hill Water Treatment Plant, a low chlorine residual alarm on the filtered water main was raised on the HMI in Control Room 2 at 03:10 but no SMS or voice call reached the on-call handset. The alarm was only noticed at the 03:40 round. A second test alarm generated from the HMI at 05:30 also failed to dispatch. The dispatch console shows the messages as "queued" with no delivery receipt.

The same behaviour appears to affect the remote sites that report through Gannet Hill, including Sorrel Creek Pump Station and Kurrajong Gap Basin. Manual phone-around from the control room is in place until this is fixed. Please treat as urgent, as weekend coverage relies entirely on the dispatch service.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
Thread
---------------------------------------------------------------------

[Mon 06:14] OT Service Desk Analyst
Logged and triaged as P2. Workaround confirmed with the control room: operator to check the HMI alarm summary every 15 minutes and phone the on-call officer directly for any priority 1 alarm. Escalated to OT Systems on-call. Reminder that under the alarm management procedure, priority 1 water quality alarms must be acknowledged within 15 minutes; please record any acknowledgement delays in the shift log.

[Mon 07:02] OT Systems Engineer
Picked up. Initial check of BVW-AS-30417: service running, queue depth climbing (currently 47 messages). The dispatch service was patched on Sunday evening under change CHG-55821 from 7.3.9 to 7.4.2 as part of CAP-TEL-26. Suspect the patch, given timing. Reviewing the gateway logs now.

[Mon 08:45] OT Systems Engineer
Found it. Version 7.4.2 changed the default outbound gateway port and enforces TLS 1.2 on the SMS gateway connection. Our cellular gateway in the Clearwell Control Building comms cabinet (BVW-NW-11028) is still on the older firmware and rejects the handshake. Messages are accepted into the queue but never leave. The vendor release notes mention this under "breaking changes" but it was not picked up in the change risk assessment.

Options:
1. Roll back the dispatch service to 7.3.9 (snapshot taken before the change, roughly 20 minutes of downtime).
2. Update the cellular gateway firmware (needs a site visit to the comms cabinet and a maintenance window).
3. Temporarily set the legacy port and cipher compatibility flag in the dispatch config.

Recommend option 3 now, then option 2 within 14 days under a new change record.

[Mon 09:10] Duty Manager
Approved option 3 as an emergency change. Please raise the retrospective change record and keep the control room informed. The Water Quality Coordinator has been told about the 30-minute gap on the chlorine residual alarm for the incident register; that goes through the Water Quality Risk Committee separately.

[Mon 09:38] OT Systems Engineer
Compatibility flag applied. Queue flushed. Test alarm from Control Room 2 dispatched and acknowledged at 09:35. Remote test from Sorrel Creek Pump Station RTU dispatched at 09:36. Kurrajong Gap Basin is reporting through the backup radio link this week while the mast works continue, so its test went via the secondary path and also delivered. Emergency change recorded as CHG-55834.

[Mon 10:05] Treatment Plant Operator
Confirmed from the control room. Received the test call on the on-call handset. Standing down the 15-minute manual checks from the next shift handover.

[Mon 14:22] OT Service Desk Analyst
Status moved to "Monitoring". Will hold open for 24 hours to confirm overnight dispatch before resolving.

[Tue 07:15] OT Systems Engineer
Overnight review: 11 alarms dispatched, all delivered with receipts, median delivery time under 40 seconds. No queue backlog.

Follow-up work for the gateway firmware: site visit to the comms cabinet booked under work order WO-20931. Note for the field crew: the access track to the Sorrel Creek Pump Station RTU kiosk is closed for culvert works, so use the public car park at the Sorrel Creek Rail Trail trailhead and walk in along the fence line. The kiosk key is in the key safe at the Clearwell Control Building reception.

[Tue 11:40] OT Change Coordinator
Both CHG-55821 and CHG-55834 added to the agenda of the Operational Technology Change Advisory Board meeting on Thursday 14 May 2026 (Boardroom B, Riverside Administration Centre, and online). The post-implementation review should cover:
- why the vendor breaking change was missed in the risk assessment;
- whether firmware dependencies of field gateways are captured in the CAP-TEL-26 asset register;
- adding an end-to-end dispatch test (HMI to handset) to the standard post-patch checklist for alarm services.

The Telemetry Renewal Project Manager has been asked to attend. The summary will also go to the Asset Management Steering Committee in the June round, because the gateway replacement may need to move forward in the capital program.

[Tue 16:20] OT Service Desk Analyst
Resolved. Root cause: TLS and port incompatibility between alarm dispatch 7.4.2 and cellular gateway firmware. Workaround: compatibility flag (CHG-55834). Permanent fix: gateway firmware update under WO-20931, target within 14 days. Ticket remains linked to the CAB review; please reopen if any dispatch failure recurs before the firmware update.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

Change (emergency): CHG-55834
Work order: WO-20931
Vendor support case: VND-77310 (opened Mon 08:50, awaiting firmware compatibility statement)

Southern Tarns Parks and Wildlife Service
People and Culture: Frequently Asked Questions
Health, Disability, Faith, Criminal History Checks and Union Matters

This FAQ supports the Workforce Wellbeing and Inclusion Policy, which takes effect on 1 July 2026. All field and office staff should read it within 30 days of that date. Managers should discuss it at their next team meeting.

1. Do I have to tell my manager about a health condition?

No. Staff are not required to disclose a health condition unless it affects their ability to work safely, for example on remote walking tracks, boat patrols or fire-ground duties. If you choose to disclose, the information goes only to the People and Culture Manager and is stored separately from your general personnel file. Your Ranger in Charge is told only about any duties that need adjusting, never the diagnosis.

2. How do I request a reasonable adjustment for a disability?

Fill in the adjustment request form on the intranet. The Service aims to respond within 14 days. Examples include modified field kit, alternative communication devices at the Pinecliff Ranger Station, or flexible start times. Adjustments are reviewed every 12 months, or sooner if your duties change. General questions about access can go to the Accessibility and Inclusion Working Group.

3. Can I take time off for religious observance?

Yes. Staff may swap rostered days or use flexible hours for religious holidays and observances. During Ramadan, for example, crew leaders can arrange lighter physical duties in the afternoon or adjusted break times where operations allow. Please give at least 2 weeks' notice for roster changes in peak season (December to February). A quiet room is available at the Mount Corrow Visitor Centre for prayer or reflection.

4. When is a criminal history check required?

A national police check is required for roles that involve working with children (school education programs, junior ranger days) or handling cash and firearms. Checks are renewed every 3 years. A record does not automatically rule anyone out: the Workforce Integrity Officer assesses relevance to the role and the outcome is kept confidential. Results are destroyed 6 months after the assessment is complete.

5. Will joining a union affect my employment?

No. Membership of a union is your choice and is never recorded on your personnel file. Union representatives may attend consultation meetings, and the Joint Consultative Committee meets quarterly to discuss rosters, fire-season overtime and field safety. Agreements made there are published on the intranet within 10 working days.

6. What wellbeing training is available?

All staff working in isolated locations complete the Remote Field Safety and Wellbeing Course within their first 90 days. Supervisors also complete the Peer Support Contact Training every 2 years. During Mental Health Week the Service runs short sessions at each regional depot.

7. Who can I contact?

For confidential advice, call the People and Culture line on (08) 7010 9379 (weekdays, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm) or write to peopleandculture@southerntarns.example. Concerns about how this policy is applied can be raised with the Workplace Health and Safety Committee. The policy will be reviewed by 30 June 2027, 12 months after it commences.

Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network
Staff Inclusion, Wellbeing and Pre-Employment Checks: Frequently Asked Questions
Document reference: 40271853 | Owner: Privacy Officer

This FAQ explains how The Kestrel Plains Network handles health, disability, faith and union matters, and how pre-employment checks work. It describes general policy only. It applies at every campus, including Corella Downs Base Hospital and our community health centres.

1. Does a staff member have to tell us about a health condition or disability?
No. Disclosure is voluntary. Staff who would like a reasonable adjustment, such as modified duties, assistive equipment or a change to rostering, can raise it with their Nurse Unit Manager or line manager. Any information shared is held on a confidential file and is not placed on the general personnel record. The Disability Inclusion Advisory Committee reviews our adjustment processes each year. Its review runs alongside Disability Access Audit Month.

2. Who needs a criminal record check, and what happens if something is disclosed?
All new employees, volunteers and student placements complete a National Police Check before they start. Roles in aged care and with children also need the relevant screening clearance. A disclosable outcome does not lead to automatic exclusion. The recruitment panel looks at how relevant it is to the inherent requirements of the role, and the applicant always has a chance to respond. Questions can go to careers@kestrelplainshealth.example.

3. Can rosters take religious observance into account?
Yes, where operational needs allow. Requests are handled like any other flexible-work request. The Pastoral Care Coordinator can advise on quiet spaces and on cultural and faith-based leave. The Faith and Pastoral Care Committee oversees this guidance.

4. Does the network record union membership?
No. Union membership is a private matter. We hold payroll deduction details only when a staff member asks for a deduction to be set up. Consultation with employee representatives happens through the Union Consultative Committee.

5. What support is there for mental health?
Staff can use the Employee Assistance Program free of charge and in confidence. Each October we hold the Mental Health Week Community Walk, and managers are encouraged to complete TRN-1210 Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials before handling any wellbeing conversation.

6. Is this information available in other languages?
Yes. Translated summaries are available on request. A Russian summary is reproduced below:

«Сотрудники KPCN не обязаны сообщать работодателю сведения о состоянии здоровья, инвалидности, религиозных убеждениях или членстве в профсоюзе. Проверка на наличие судимости проводится для всех новых сотрудников и волонтёров, но её результат не означает автоматического отказа. Вопросы можно направить по адресу careers@kestrelplainshealth.example.»

7. Who can I contact about privacy?
Email privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example or call 1300 975 707 during business hours. Concerns about how personal information has been handled are acknowledged within 5 business days.

This FAQ is reviewed annually by the Director of Clinical Governance and the Privacy Officer.

MOORABOOL METALFORMING PTY LTD
North Geelong Pressing Plant — 14 Kilnworth Drive, North Geelong VIC 3215

Quarterly Report: Machine Guarding and Lockout/Tagout Compliance Review
Reporting period: Q1 2026
Report reference: RPT-SAF-2026-01
Prepared by: Site Safety Coordinator
Reviewed by: Plant Operations Manager
Tabled at: Joint Health and Safety Committee, meeting of 18 March 2026, Training Room B

---

1. Executive summary

This report sets out the results of the first-quarter review of machine guarding and isolation practice across the three production halls at the North Geelong Pressing Plant. The review covered 46 fixed and mobile assets, 212 lockout events logged in the maintenance system and 31 open maintenance tickets with a guarding or isolation element.

Overall compliance with the site isolation procedure rose from 88 per cent in Q4 2025 to 93 per cent this quarter. Two findings are rated high: interlock faults on the 400-tonne transfer press and incomplete isolation points on the coil feed line. Neither caused an injury. Both have been contained with interim controls and have corrective actions assigned to roles, with due dates set out in Section 5.

The review was carried out under the consultation arrangements agreed in the site enterprise agreement. Health and Safety Representatives from each shift were invited to every walk-through. Consultation took place through the Joint Health and Safety Committee and the Shop Floor Consultative Forum.

2. Scope

In scope:
- Hall A: progressive die presses and the PRS-0042 transfer press cell
- Hall B: coil feed, decoiler and straightener line (CFL-0107)
- Hall C: robotic spot-weld cells and the end-of-line inspection station
- The Tool Room and the Die Maintenance Bay

Out of scope: the warehouse, the dispatch dock and office areas. These are covered by the separate traffic management review, RPT-SAF-2026-02.

3. Method

The review combined four sources of evidence:

a) Physical inspection of each asset against the guarding checklist FRM-GD-07, carried out on scheduled walk-throughs every Tuesday and Thursday between 06:30 and 08:00 so that all three shift crossovers were observed.
b) Extraction of lockout events from the computerised maintenance management system, version 7.4.2, which was upgraded during the quarter from 7.3.9.
c) Review of interlock diagnostic logs downloaded from press controllers running firmware 3.18.0.
d) Structured toolbox discussions in the Hall B Crib Room. Feedback was recorded by theme only, with no attribution.

Each finding was rated High, Medium or Low against the site risk matrix. A High rating requires an interim control within 24 hours and a permanent fix within 30 days.

4. Findings

4.1 Transfer press interlocks (High)
The light curtain on the rear access of PRS-0042 showed intermittent fault resets on 14 occasions during the quarter. The controller log shows that the press did not cycle during any fault. However, the reset sequence could be completed without a second-person verification. Maintenance ticket MNT-40817 was raised and the rear access was physically barricaded as an interim control. The replacement curtain is on order under purchase order PO-118204.

4.2 Coil feed line isolation points (High)
Three of eleven energy sources on CFL-0107 (pneumatic accumulator, hydraulic straightener and the decoiler brake) were not labelled on the isolation board. Lockout events on this line most often recorded "electrical only". Ticket MNT-40852 covers the relabelling. The isolation procedure card ISO-CFL-03 is being reissued.

4.3 Spot-weld cell gate switches (Medium)
Two gate switches in Hall C had been fitted with spare actuators, which allowed bypass. The actuators were removed on the day they were found and logged under MNT-40866. The Maintenance Planner has added a quarterly actuator audit to the preventive schedule.

4.4 Lock and tag stock (Low)
Personal lock stations in Hall A and Hall B were below minimum stock at four of twelve checks. A reorder trigger has been set in the stores system.

4.5 Training currency (Medium)
Of the roles that require isolation competency, 91 per cent were current at quarter end. The remaining refreshers are scheduled within 6 weeks in Training Room B under course TRN-LOTO-02, Isolation and Lockout Refresher.

4.6 Positive practice
Toolbox feedback across all shifts reported strong support for the new shadow board layout in the Die Maintenance Bay and for the colour-coded isolation tags trialled in Hall A. Near-miss reporting rose by 22 per cent, which the committee treats as a healthy reporting culture.

5. Corrective actions

| Action | Owner (role) | Ticket | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replace rear light curtain, add two-person reset | Maintenance Superintendent | MNT-40817 | within 30 days |
| Relabel coil line isolation board | Electrical Leading Hand | MNT-40852 | within 14 days |
| Quarterly gate actuator audit | Maintenance Planner | MNT-40866 | ongoing |
| Complete overdue refreshers | Training and Compliance Officer | MNT-40871 | within 6 weeks |

Progress will be reported at the next Joint Health and Safety Committee meeting on 15 April 2026. A follow-up walk-through is planned for the Wednesday of the same week.

6. Consultation note

Under the site agreement, draft findings were circulated to Health and Safety Representatives at least 7 days before tabling. They were also provided to the union consultative group through the Shop Floor Consultative Forum. No objections were lodged. Two suggestions were adopted: extending the walk-through window to cover the afternoon shift start, and adding a lockout question to the daily pre-start checklist.

---

Appendix A: Asset register extract (in-scope assets with findings)

| Asset tag | Description | Hall | Controller firmware |
|---|---|---|---|
| PRS-0042 | 400 t transfer press | A | 3.18.0 |
| CFL-0107 | Coil feed and straightener line | B | 2.9.4 |
| WLD-0213 | Robotic spot-weld cell 3 | C | 5.1.1 |
| WLD-0214 | Robotic spot-weld cell 4 | C | 5.1.1 |

Appendix B: Walk-through schedule, Q1 2026

| Week | Day | Area | Attendance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | Tuesday | Hall A, Tool Room | Safety Coordinator, HSR (rostered shift) |
| 1–4 | Thursday | Hall B, Hall C | Safety Coordinator, HSR (rostered shift) |
| 5–13 | Tuesday / Thursday | Rotating | As above, plus Maintenance Planner |

Appendix C: Distribution

Copies go to the Plant Operations Manager, the Maintenance Superintendent and members of the Joint Health and Safety Committee. A copy is also posted on the safety noticeboard outside the Hall B Crib Room. Questions about this report should go to the safety mailbox, safety@moorabool-metalforming.example.

text:
THE NIGHT YARD

Chapter Four: Thursday

The B-doubles started rolling in off the Hume Highway a little after two, their headlights sweeping across the wet bitumen of the Bellwether Freight Lines yard like slow searchlights. Ray Kostakis watched them from the window of the dispatch hut. A mug of instant coffee was going cold in his hand.

He had been back eleven weeks. Before that, he had served three years in prison over a trailer of cigarettes that vanished somewhere between two depots. He still swore he had never touched the job. Nobody at the yard asked about it, which was its own kind of asking.

The roster was thin. Half the drivers had taken the long weekend before Anzac Day, and the ones who stayed had the look of men who wanted the overtime more than the sleep. Dock 6 was still blocked by a pallet of split cement bags. Somebody had chalked BACK SOON on the forklift, and nobody believed it.

At ten past three the side door banged and Noor Haddad came in out of the drizzle, shaking water off her hi-vis. She was the night supervisor, younger than half the men she supervised and sharper than all of them. She dropped a clipboard on the desk without looking at him.

"Linehaul from the north is forty minutes late," she said. "Brakes, apparently. You believe that?"

"I believe brakes fail," Ray said.

She gave him a long look, the kind she gave a manifest that did not add up. Then she went to her locker at the back of the hut. She took out the folded prayer mat she kept there and knelt to pray facing the roller doors, as she did every night when the hour came round. The radio crackled with somebody's reversing beeps. Ray turned the volume down without being asked. He had learned in the last three years which silences belonged to other people.

When she stood again the yard lights had changed colour, the way they did when the generator kicked over. Out past the fence a single truck idled with its lights off. It was not on any sheet he had seen.

"That one yours?" Noor asked.

"Not mine," he said. "Not anyone's, by the look of it."

She picked up the torch. He picked up his jacket. Neither of them reached for the phone. Later, when the police came and the questions started, that was the part he kept coming back to: how easily they had both decided not to call it in.

Out in the rain, the idling truck began, very slowly, to move.

Corio Bay Extrusions - Maintenance & Facilities Service Desk
==============================================================

Ticket: MNT-30412
Linked case: CS-24871
Status: Open - Awaiting Consultation
Priority: P2 (Safety-related, production impact)
Site: North Shore Plant
Location: Press Hall 2, Line 4
Asset: PRS-07-0193 (800 t hydraulic extrusion press)
Requested by: Production Shift Supervisor (B shift)
Assigned to: Maintenance Planner
Notify: maintenance@coriobayextrusions.example; ohs@coriobayextrusions.example
Category: Guarding / Interlocks

Summary
-------
The rear light-curtain interlock on press 7 trips at random during die changes. The trip leaves the press in a safe state each time, but it causes repeated stoppages. B shift has logged 11 trips over 5 shifts. The press is running under a temporary procedure, with a second person present for every die change.

Thread
------

[Mon 06:42] Production Shift Supervisor:
Trips are getting more frequent and now happen roughly every 40 minutes. The operators are following the interim procedure. Please confirm whether the line can keep running or should come down for the guard inspection.

[Mon 08:15] Maintenance Planner:
Logged against the existing CS-24871 because this is the second interlock fault on this asset this quarter. The electrical crew will inspect the receiver alignment and the safety relay today. The replacement relay (part SR-4410) has a lead time of 10 business days. If the relay is at fault, the earliest fit is the long weekend shutdown around Anzac Day, 25 April 2026.

[Mon 13:30] Electrical Maintenance Lead:
Receiver alignment checked and within tolerance. The safety relay shows intermittent contact bounce and needs replacing. The relay has been ordered. Until then the interim two-person procedure stays in place. It will be reviewed every 24 hours.

[Tue 07:05] OHS Coordinator:
Risk assessment updated and attached. The control is acceptable for a maximum of 21 days. Fitting the relay over the Anzac Day shutdown means a roster change for the maintenance crew. Under the enterprise agreement, roster changes need consultation with employee representatives at least 7 days before they take effect. I have put this on the agenda of the Joint Consultative Committee meeting on Thursday 16 April 2026 in Training Room B.

[Tue 09:48] Plant Manager:
Approved in principle, subject to the consultation outcome. Please also raise the press guarding audit at the same meeting. The committee asked for the audit results within 3 months of the last incident review.

[Wed 11:20] Maintenance Planner:
Draft shutdown plan circulated to maintenance@coriobayextrusions.example:
- Isolate press 7 and the Line 4 hydraulics: 4 hours
- Replace the safety relay and test the light curtain: 3 hours
- Run the verification test and sign-off by the OHS Coordinator: 2 hours
Total crew time is about 9 hours. The plan relies on the relay arriving at least 48 hours before the shutdown.

[Wed 15:02] Stores Officer:
Supplier confirms dispatch. Expected delivery is within 8 business days.

Next actions
------------
1. Present the roster change and the guarding audit at the Joint Consultative Committee meeting on Thursday 16 April 2026.
2. Confirm the relay is received and booked in by Stores.
3. Review the interim two-person procedure every 24 hours. Escalate if trips exceed 15 per shift.
4. Close MNT-30412 after the post-repair verification. Keep CS-24871 open for 90 days of monitoring.

Please send all correspondence on this ticket to maintenance@coriobayextrusions.example, not to individual inboxes.

File note: Welfare and conduct matter
Organisation: Brightquill Labs (People & Culture, APAC/UK)
Case reference: PC-2026-0417
Prepared by: Ines Kovačević, People Partner (Sydney)
Classification: Confidential, People & Culture only

1. Background

Mere Tawhiri (Senior Backend Engineer, Auckland) contacted People & Culture after a cross-team video stand-up held on 7 May 2026. Mere reports that during the informal part of the call, Callum Rourke (Engineering Lead, Manchester) referred to her private life in front of eleven attendees. Mere confirmed to me that she is bisexual. She had told only a small number of colleagues and had not chosen to share this with the wider team. She described the comment as humiliating and said she logged off early.

2. Meeting with Mere

A support meeting was held by video on 14 May 2026, with Daniel Achterberg (Head of Platform) also attending. Mere was offered the Employee Assistance Program and accepted the details. She asked that the matter be handled formally but without a group-wide announcement. She also confirmed that she still wants to go ahead with her planned internal transfer to the Sydney team. This transfer was agreed before the incident and is not connected to it.

3. Response from Callum

Callum was interviewed separately. He accepted that he made the remark and said he "assumed everyone already knew". He said he is not gay and "didn't think it was the sort of thing people keep quiet any more". He apologised and agreed to complete the respectful-workplace module. Daniel will speak with him about expectations for team calls.

4. Transfer administration (for Payroll, held on this file at Mere's request)

Mere has asked that her relocation paperwork be processed through this case so that she only has to deal with one contact.
- Current address: Flat 3, 28 Kōwhai Terrace, Grey Lynn, Auckland 1021
- New address from transfer: Unit 12, 45 Wattle Lane, Marrickville NSW 2204
- Australian TFN supplied: 784 246 584
- Identity verification: NSW driver licence 53891776 (sighted by video)
- Proposed Sydney start: 1 July 2026

Mere mentioned that she is keen to use the Sydney co-working space near Circular Quay on her in-office days.

5. Outcome and next steps

An outcome letter dated 22 May 2026 will be issued to both parties. It will confirm the finding of a breach of the Respectful Workplace Policy, the agreed remedial training and a 90-day check-in. Mere will be offered a follow-up conversation with me within 2 weeks of the letter. Payroll is to destroy the copy of the licence scan once the address change and TFN declaration are complete.

Reviewed: Daniel Achterberg

HALBURY COASTAL BANK LIMITED
People and Culture | Employee Relations
RESTRICTED CASE FILE NOTE: EMPLOYEE SAFETY, WELLBEING AND PAYROLL INTEGRITY

Case ticket: PCS-0047213
Case category: Wellbeing and safety (restricted), with a linked payroll integrity check
Access: case owner, escalation point, Site Security Lead and Payroll Integrity only. Do not copy to the general HR inbox. Do not attach to the performance or capability record.

Employee: Thanaporn Toyorta (prefers Tida)
Employee number: HCB-E40871
Position: Payments Exceptions Analyst, Payments Operations, Level 3
Work location: Bellbird Terrace Operations Centre, Adelaide
Line manager: Desmond Achterberg
Case owner and author: Bridget Kowalczyk
Escalation point: Head of Employee Relations
Status: Open. Active safety plan. Review at four weeks.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
1. PURPOSE OF THIS NOTE
-----------------------------------------------------------------

This note records four things. The first is a disclosure an employee made to me. The second is the support the bank has put in place. The third is an attempted change to her payroll details that we believe someone other than her made. The fourth is the re-check of her identity and personal details that followed. Anyone who picks up the case while I am away should be able to understand what has been agreed without asking the employee to repeat her story. Please read the whole note before you contact her.

Two principles apply throughout. First, nothing in this note is to be discussed with the Payments Operations team beyond what is set out in section 7. Second, her new home address and contact details are held only here and in the restricted Payroll Integrity record. They are not to be entered into the HR system, the roster tool or the building access system until she tells us otherwise in writing.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
2. ENTRY 1, Mon 09:40, Quiet Room 3B, Level 3
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Present: Tida, myself. Desmond joined for the last ten minutes at her request.

Desmond Achterberg rang me at 08:55. He said Tida had asked him for a private conversation first thing and he thought it should be with People and Culture. He was right to call. He did not ask her for details and told her she could choose who she spoke to. I met her in Quiet Room 3B at 09:40 and we spoke for about an hour.

Tida told me she left the house she shared with her former partner after he smashed her phone against the kitchen wall and locked her out in the driveway on the night of 21 February 2026. Her former partner is Samhan Martota. They are not married. They lived together for a little over four years.

Since then she has been staying in crisis accommodation arranged by a women's support worker. She has signed a lease on a small unit and moves in at the end of this week. I told her that Desmond completed the Family Violence Awareness for People Leaders module with the other Level 3 team leaders last year. He would therefore understand why she might need to leave the floor at short notice. She was relieved to hear this. She said she wanted him to know the basics but not the detail.

She described what life had been like at home. In her words, he "kept my bank card and checked every payment I made", and if she bought lunch with colleagues he would ask why. Her pay went into a joint account that he managed. She did not have her own online banking login until two weeks ago. I record this here because it is directly relevant to Entry 2.

She now has an interim intervention order against him, granted on 26 February 2026. She showed me the order on her phone. I did not take a copy. The order covers her workplace. I have asked her to email me a copy from her personal address when she feels ready, so that Security can see the conditions. I explained that it will be stored only in the restricted folder.

She said she was also worried about his history. In her words: "Samhan did two years inside before I met him. He told me it was a mistake and that he had changed." She said he has a criminal record for dishonesty offences, including using other people's identity documents. This is why she fears he will contact the bank and pretend to be her or claim to act for her. I have not checked any of this, and we do not need to check it to act on her safety. I record it because it shaped the payroll controls in section 4.

She also said that his younger brother, who is on parole, has come to her friend's house twice asking where she is. She does not think the brother knows where she works, but she cannot be sure. She has posted photos from the bank's community day in the past.

On support, I explained the Employee Assistance Program, which is provided by Morrowgate Employee Support. She could refer herself, or I could make the call with her. Tida grew up in Khon Kaen and speaks Isan with her family and asked whether a Thai-speaking counsellor is available. I rang the provider's intake line during the meeting. They confirmed they can arrange a Thai-speaking counsellor by telehealth within a week, and she accepted. She asked for the Thai spelling of her name to be used on the referral, as her mother will help her with paperwork. She writes it as ธนพร โทยอร์ตา. Her mother, สมใจ, is flying in from Thailand next week to stay with her for a month.

We talked about her routines. She takes food to the monks at the wat every Sunday morning. She said this is the one place she is worried about, because Samhan used to drive her there and knows when she arrives. That is outside work and outside our control. I gave her the police liaison number from her order paperwork and suggested she raise it with her support worker as part of her own safety plan.

When Desmond joined, we agreed together:
- Ten days of paid special leave, starting next Monday (see section 6).
- No change to her role or her queue. She does not want to move to another team.
- Flexible start and finish times on her return.
- Desmond will tell the team only that Tida is taking some leave for personal reasons.

Tida said she felt better for having told someone at work. She left the meeting at 10:45 and chose to go back to her desk.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
3. ENTRY 2, Tue 10:52, call to the Payroll Services line
-----------------------------------------------------------------

At 10:52 Lachlan Pyke in Payroll Services took a call from a man. He said he was calling "on behalf of my wife, Thanaporn". He said she was unwell and could not call herself, and that her pay needed to go into a new account from the next pay run. He gave her full name, employee number and date of birth correctly. He then gave a BSB and account number that do not match anything we hold for her.

Lachlan followed the call-back procedure. He told the caller that only the employee can change bank details, either through the self-service portal or in person with photo identification, and he ended the call. The caller became abusive and said he would "come in and sort it out". Lachlan logged the call with Payroll Integrity straight away and copied me. I had placed a "contact People and Culture before any change" flag on her file the afternoon before.

Between 11:20 and 13:05 the Payments Operations team mailbox received three emails from samhan_martota98@example.net. The first asked for Tida's roster for the next fortnight. The second asked which car park she uses. The third said he was "her partner and next of kin" and that the bank had no right to keep her details from him. Nobody replied. Desmond read only the subject lines, forwarded all three to me and then deleted them from the team mailbox. I have saved them to the restricted folder and blocked the sender at mailbox level.

I rang Tida at 13:30 to tell her. She said she was not surprised. She believes the caller was Samhan, who she says controlled all of her money while they lived together and took her pay as soon as it landed. She had already opened an account at another institution. She had meant to update her details through the portal but had not done so, because she feared he still had access to her old phone and would see the confirmation text. We agreed to make the change in person, with identification, the next day.

I asked whether she wanted the bank to report the call and emails to police. She said she would report them herself to the officer handling her order. She asked us to keep the call log and the emails in case they are needed. Security has also been told (see section 5).

-----------------------------------------------------------------
4. ENTRY 3, Wed 14:00, identity re-verification and personal details update
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Present: Tida, Lachlan Pyke (Payroll Services), myself. Held in Interview Room 2, Level 1, away from the Payments floor.

The caller in Entry 2 knew her employee number and date of birth. We therefore treated every existing detail on her payroll record as possibly compromised. We re-verified her from documents rather than from knowledge questions. Lachlan viewed the originals and recorded the numbers. We kept no copies beyond what the tax and super forms require.

Documents viewed:
- Australian passport K3973687 (original sighted, photo matched)
- South Australian driver's licence 28379823 (original sighted; the card shows her old address and she will update it after she moves)
- Medicare card 6642 77406 3 (sighted as a secondary document)
- New TFN declaration lodged in person, tax file number 127 453 154, matched to the number already on file
- She worked in hospitality in Honolulu for three years before moving to Adelaide and still receives a small payment from a US retirement plan. Her foreign income declaration therefore carries her US Social Security number, 987-65-4326. She confirmed it and asked that it stay as it is.

Date of birth confirmed: 4 August 1993.

Bank details: her salary will now be paid into her own account at another institution, BSB and account 999-188 46282825. She logged into her new online banking on her own phone in front of us to show the account name. Lachlan made the change in the payroll system while she watched. The joint account has been removed from her record entirely.

New contact details: mobile 0491 572 363 (new number and new handset, not known to her former partner). Personal email for all HR and payroll correspondence while she is on leave: t.toyorta@example.org. The old mobile number has been deleted from her record and from the emergency contact list.

She has asked that her new address be kept off every bank system that he could see or that could ever be released to him. I agreed. The new address is recorded below for Security and emergency use only. It is not to be typed into the HR system, the roster tool, the access control system or any letter template. Correspondence goes to her personal email. If a letter must be posted, it goes care of me at Level 3 for her to collect.

Personal details update, restricted extract

| Field | Recorded value |
|---|---|
| Legal name | Thanaporn Toyorta |
| Preferred name | Tida |
| Name in Thai script | ธนพร โทยอร์ตา |
| Employee number | HCB-E40871 |
| Date of birth | 4 August 1993 |
| Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin | No |
| Residential address (restricted) | Unit 6, 18 Parakeet Close, Tullara Park SA 5097 |
| Previous address (to be removed) | 27 Gidgee Street, Wyndara Grove SA 5112 |
| Mobile | 0491 572 363 |
| Personal email | t.toyorta@example.org |
| Emergency contact | Removed at employee's request; new contact to be added when her mother arrives |
| Bank account for salary | 999-188 46282825 |

The previous emergency contact on her file was Samhan Martota. That entry has been deleted. The previous address on her file, 27 Gidgee Street, Wyndara Grove SA 5112, is the home she left and has been removed from the active record. Payroll will keep it only in the history table, which managers cannot see.

Lachlan has added a Payroll Integrity marker to her record. Any request to change her bank details, address, phone or email, by any channel, now needs one of two things: her in person with photo ID, or a video call with me where she shows ID on camera. Phone and email requests are declined without exception, even if the caller has correct details.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
5. SAFETY PLAN AT SITE
-----------------------------------------------------------------

I briefed Ruairi Feeney, Site Security Lead, on Wednesday afternoon. I gave him only what he needs:
- the name and a recent photo of Samhan Martota, which Tida provided and agreed to share
- the fact that an order is in place that covers the workplace
- the abusive call to Payroll and the three emails.

I did not share her new address with him. I only confirmed that Security holds it in the restricted record for emergencies.

Agreed site measures:
- Reception at Bellbird Terrace Operations Centre will not confirm to any caller or visitor whether she works here. The standard script applies: "We cannot confirm whether a person works here, but I can pass on a message."
- Security has the photo at the ground floor desk and in the control room. If he is seen on site or in the car park, Security will call police first, then Ruairi, then me.
- Her parking has moved from the open-air lot to the basement, which has controlled entry. Her access card has been reissued with a new number.
- She can ask Security to walk her to her car at any time without giving a reason.
- Her desk stays where it is, but her name has been removed from the floor plan on the Level 3 noticeboard and from the printed team phone list.
- Her work calendar is set to private.

Ruairi has also asked the contract cleaning and catering providers, without naming her, to report anyone who asks about staff rosters or arrival times.

The site measures are reviewed with the Site Security Manager every fortnight while the case is open.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
6. LEAVE AND RETURN
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Tida is on paid special leave from 2 March 2026 to 13 March 2026 inclusive. The payroll system codes this as "special leave, personal", and her manager and the rostering team cannot see the reason. The confirmation letter dated 27 February 2026 went to her personal email, t.toyorta@example.org, not to her work inbox.

The leave gives her time to move house, attend court and appointments, and settle her mother in. If she needs more, she has my number and can call. She has been told she does not need to provide documents to extend the leave. We agreed a short phone check-in in the middle of each week while she is away. The call comes from me, not from her manager, unless she asks otherwise.

On return:
- First week: 10:00 to 15:00, then her normal hours, adjusted as she needs.
- She keeps her queue and her role.
- On her first morning back, a return meeting with me and Desmond in Quiet Room 3B. We will check that the site measures are working and confirm what the team has been told.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
7. TEAM AND COLLEAGUE CONSIDERATIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------

The team has been told only that Tida is on leave for personal reasons and that her work will be covered. Desmond will handle any questions himself.

Cover for her exceptions queue will be split between Amira Haddad and Kenji Oyelaran. When Desmond asked Amira about extra hours, she said she is fasting until sunset through Ramadan this month and would prefer to start at 07:00 and finish early rather than stay late. That is fine and has been approved as a separate, routine roster change. It is noted here only because it affects the cover arrangement. Kenji will cover the afternoon cut-off window.

Neither colleague has been told anything about the circumstances. As standard practice for the whole team, Desmond has told them that if they receive a call or email asking about Tida, they should say nothing and forward it to him.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
8. GOVERNANCE AND REPORTING
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Payroll Integrity has recorded the attempted bank detail change as a near-miss for payroll fraud, without the employee's name, against the case ticket PCS-0047213.

A de-identified summary (no names, no site detail) will go to the Respect and Safety at Work Committee for its 24 March 2026 meeting, as part of the quarterly trend report on staff safety. The point for the committee is the control gap. The caller had the employee number and date of birth, which our phone procedure once accepted as enough. Payroll has already tightened the script. The committee should consider whether to drop knowledge-based verification for all staff.

Nothing in this case is to be raised in any performance discussion. Desmond has confirmed he understands that he must not raise any drop in her queue numbers over this period with her.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
9. ACTIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------

| # | Action | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Restricted marker on HR and payroll record; no changes by phone or email | LP | Done |
| 2 | Remove old address, old mobile and former emergency contact from active record | LP | Done |
| 3 | Brief Security; photo at front desk; basement parking; new access card | RF | Done |
| 4 | EAP referral with Thai-speaking counsellor | BK | Done, first session booked |
| 5 | Mid-week check-in calls while on leave | BK | Ongoing |
| 6 | Tell team about leave in neutral terms; arrange queue cover | DA | Done |
| 7 | Request copy of order conditions when she is ready; file in restricted folder | BK | Open |
| 8 | Preserve call log and three emails for possible police request | BK | Done |
| 9 | De-identified near-miss summary to committee | BK | Open |
| 10 | Return meeting on first morning back | BK / DA | Open |

-----------------------------------------------------------------
10. NOTES FOR ANYONE COVERING THIS CASE
-----------------------------------------------------------------

- Call her only on her new mobile. Do not leave detailed voicemails. Say who you are and ask her to call People and Culture back.
- Do not email her work address about this matter.
- If anyone calls asking for her, do not confirm she works here, whoever they say they are (partner, family, police, lawyer, another bank). Take a message and a call-back number and tell me or the Head of Employee Relations.
- If she tells you she is unsafe right now, call police first.
- She has been clear that she wants to keep working and does not want to be treated as fragile. Please respect that.

Entry recorded by Bridget Kowalczyk, People and Culture, Halbury Coastal Bank Limited. Read back to Tida by phone on Thursday at 16:10. She confirmed it is accurate and asked for one change, the spelling of her mother's name, which has been made.

Next review: four weeks from opening, or sooner if anything changes.

TIDEWELL WORKPLACE HEALTH
Employee Assistance Program: Clinical Progress Note and Workplace Referral
Contracted EAP provider to Lanternfish Systems (remote-first; Sydney, Auckland and Manchester hubs)

CONFIDENTIAL: CLINICAL RECORD. Only Section 6 may be released to the employer, with the client's consent.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Session details
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Client:                 Mereana Tautahi
Employer staff no.:     LF-E30417
EAP client no.:         TWH-C58210
Referral reference:     EAP-REF-58201
Session:                3 of 6 approved (telehealth, video)
Session date:           12 March 2026, 10:00 to 10:55 AEDT
Clinician:              Ines Valdivia, Clinical Psychologist
Referred by:            Line manager Callum Deegan (staff no. LF-E11826), via People Support ticket PPL-30471

Consent: At the start of the session the limits of confidentiality were explained again. The client consented to the workplace recommendations in Section 6 being sent to her line manager and to People Support. She did not consent to the release of any other part of this note.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Subjective
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Mereana is a senior backend engineer on the payments platform team. She works fully remotely from regional Victoria and has been with the employer for about four years. She first disclosed the matter in session 2, and today she confirmed that she is experiencing family violence from her former partner, who is now the subject of an interim intervention order. She has moved house since our last session. At her request the new residential address is recorded here only and is not to be passed to the employer:

    Unit 2, 41 Marrong Street, Tarrabee VIC 3361

She reports that over the past six weeks work has felt "like the one normal thing left". She also finds it hard to concentrate during long incident calls. She has been seeing her GP for anxiety and broken sleep. She is attending those appointments and describes the GP as supportive. She denies any thoughts of self-harm and was able to name clear reasons for living and a number of supports.

Mereana describes her whānau as her main support. She goes home to her marae on the East Coast for tangihanga and whānau hui. She would like to know that she can step away from work at short notice for those occasions without having to explain why each time.

She raised a specific worry about a pre-employment-style screening. The employer's government health-records customer requires a fresh national police check for every engineer with production access. Mereana feared that the court process would "show up against me". We discussed that being the protected person in intervention order proceedings does not create a record against her. She confirmed that she has no criminal record. Her concern is mainly about privacy, because she does not want the customer's compliance staff to learn anything about her circumstances.

She has an adjustments meeting coming up with Callum. She would like a support person present. In her words: "I joined the tech workers' guild when the enterprise agreement talks started, so I'd like Hemi there with me." Hemi Paraone is a platform engineer based in Sydney who is the elected bargaining delegate for the engineering staff. Mereana says she trusts him to keep the discussion focused on practical arrangements.

Callum had first proposed meeting in person in the Kauri Room at the Auckland hub. Mereana does not want to travel at present, and the meeting will now be held by video.

She shared an email from Callum with me. In it he notes that the Manchester support team lead, who is the shop steward for the support floor there, has offered to swap overnight on-call blocks with the payments team. The aim is to take Mereana off the public pager roster for the next quarter. She was relieved to hear this.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Objective / Mental state
--------------------------------------------------------------------
- Appearance and engagement: Appropriately presented, on camera throughout, and engaged well.
- Speech: Normal rate and volume.
- Mood and affect: Mood described as "tired but steadier". Affect was reactive, and she was tearful briefly when discussing the move.
- Thought content: Preoccupied with safety and privacy. No perceptual disturbance noted.
- Insight and judgement: Good.
- Measures: The K10 was repeated today. Her score has reduced since session 1 and now sits in the moderate range.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Assessment
--------------------------------------------------------------------
She is under significant psychosocial stress, which is linked to her personal safety circumstances and to the visibility of her work schedule. Her protective factors are strong: whānau support, engaged GP care, a meaningful job and a manager who is responsive. Her current risk to self is assessed as low. Workplace risks centre on the predictability of her working pattern, which comes from the shared calendar, the published on-call roster and her public status indicators in the chat tool.

The employer's own policy says that employees experiencing family violence can access up to ten days of paid leave each year without providing evidence. No personal leave request was discussed today.

The employer has also opened a general review of overnight on-call rosters across all teams under CASE-03417. That review is institutional and does not concern this client specifically.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Safety and contact plan (clinical record only)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
- Preferred contact: her new mobile, 0491 574 411. Her previous number is no longer in use and must not be called.
- Secondary safe contact: her sister, Aroha Tautahi, on landline (03) 5550 8573. Messages are to be left with Aroha only, with no detail about the reason for the call.
- The client already holds a copy of her safety plan from session 2. It was reviewed today and no changes were needed.
- Next session: 26 March 2026, telehealth.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Workplace recommendations (releasable, consent given)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
To: Callum Deegan, re staff no. LF-E30417
