text:
# =============================================================================
#  relay-gateway :: deploy/environments/production.yaml
#
#  Consumed by:   brackenctl deploy (internal release tool, pipeline stage 4)
#  Owner team:    Platform Engineering, Brackenfold Systems
#  Escalation:    platform-oncall@brackenfold.example
#  Change ref:    CHG-418833 (approved at the Change Advisory Board)
#
#  DO NOT COMMIT SECRET VALUES TO THIS FILE.
#  Every credential below is either a reference into the secret manager
#  (Keyhold, mount "kv-prod") or a template placeholder that the release
#  pipeline resolves at deploy time. The pre-commit hook
#  tools/hooks/no-literal-secrets.sh rejects anything that looks like a
#  literal key, token or password. Background and post-incident review:
#  SEC-1194.
#
#  Edits to this file need two approvals from the platform-reviewers group
#  and a linked ticket in the commit message. Rollbacks do not need a new
#  change record if they target the release listed under previousRelease.
# =============================================================================

schemaVersion: 3

organisation:
  name: "Brackenfold Systems"
  entities:
    au: "Brackenfold Systems Pty Ltd"
    nz: "Brackenfold Systems NZ Limited"
    uk: "Brackenfold Systems (UK) Ltd"
  # Shared mailboxes only. Never put an individual's address in this file;
  # on-call routing is resolved from the rota service at alert time.
  contacts:
    platform: "platform-oncall@brackenfold.example"
    security: "security-alerts@brackenfold.example"
    finance: "finance-ops@brackenfold.example"
    support: "support-escalations@brackenfold.example"
    statusPage: "status-updates@brackenfold.example"
    privacy: "privacy@brackenfold.example"

environment: production
tier: tier-1            # customer-facing, 99.95% monthly availability target

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Release
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
release:
  service: "Relay Gateway"
  component: relay-gateway
  version: "4.18.2"
  build: "20931"
  gitSha: "9f3c1e7a"
  registry: registry.brackenfold.example/platform/relay-gateway
  tag: "4.18.2-b20931"
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  # Signed artefacts only. The verifier fetches the public half of the
  # signing pair from the secret manager; the private half never leaves it.
  signature:
    required: true
    verifierKeyRef: "keyhold://kv-prod/release-signing/relay-gateway#public_key"

previousRelease:
  # Known-good rollback target. Keep this in step with the release notes in
  # docs/releases/relay-gateway.md after every promotion.
  version: "4.17.6"
  build: "20744"
  tag: "4.17.6-b20744"

canary:
  enabled: true
  initialWeightPercent: 5
  stepWeightPercent: 15
  stepIntervalMinutes: 20
  maxWeightPercent: 100
  abortOn:
    errorRatePercent: 1.5
    p99LatencyMs: 900
  # Canary build pinned separately while PLAT-3412 is open.
  candidateBuild: "20958"
  candidateVersion: "4.18.3-rc.1"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regions and cost attribution
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The company is remote-first; the three studios host edge appliances and
# a small amount of build capacity only. All customer traffic is served from
# the regional clusters.
regions:
  - id: syd
    displayName: "Sydney"
    cluster: prod-syd-01
    timezone: Australia/Sydney
    costCentre: "CC-4102"
    studio: "Wharf Six Studio"
    podCidr: 10.42.0.0/16
    serviceCidr: 10.43.0.0/20
    replicas:
      min: 6
      max: 24
    primaryForTenants: [apac-east, apac-south]
  - id: akl
    displayName: "Auckland"
    cluster: prod-akl-01
    timezone: Pacific/Auckland
    costCentre: "CC-5207"
    studio: "Tui Street Loft"
    podCidr: 10.52.0.0/16
    serviceCidr: 10.53.0.0/20
    replicas:
      min: 4
      max: 16
    primaryForTenants: [apac-nz, pacific]
  - id: man
    displayName: "Manchester"
    cluster: prod-man-01
    timezone: Europe/London
    costCentre: "CC-6311"
    studio: "Fernhook House"
    podCidr: 10.62.0.0/16
    serviceCidr: 10.63.0.0/20
    replicas:
      min: 6
      max: 20
    primaryForTenants: [emea-uk, emea-eu]

costAttribution:
  # Shared platform spend is split by request volume at month end.
  sharedCostCentre: "CC-1000"
  tagKeys:
    - bf:cost-centre
    - bf:service
    - bf:environment
  reportRecipient: "finance-ops@brackenfold.example"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Secrets (references only)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
secrets:
  provider: keyhold
  address: https://keyhold.internal.brackenfold.example:8200
  authMethod: workload-identity
  role: relay-gateway-prod
  renewBeforeExpiryMinutes: 30
  refs:
    databaseUser: "keyhold://kv-prod/relay-gateway/postgres#username"
    databasePassword: "keyhold://kv-prod/relay-gateway/postgres#password"
    cachePassword: "keyhold://kv-prod/relay-gateway/cache#auth"
    queueCredentials: "keyhold://kv-prod/relay-gateway/queue#connection"
    sessionCookieKey: "${KEYHOLD_REF:kv-prod/relay-gateway/session#cookie_key}"
    webhookSigningKey: "{{ secret \"kv-prod/relay-gateway/webhooks\" \"signing_key\" }}"
    ledgerSyncClientSecret: "{{ secret \"kv-prod/ledger-sync/clients/relay-gateway\" \"client_secret\" }}"
    billingBridgeApiKey: "keyhold://kv-prod/billing-bridge/clients/relay-gateway#api_key"
    notificationHubToken: "keyhold://kv-prod/notification-hub/clients/relay-gateway#token"
    tlsBundle: "keyhold://pki-prod/issue/relay-gateway#bundle"
  # Rotation is driven by the secret manager; the gateway reloads on SIGHUP.
  rotation:
    databasePasswordDays: 30
    apiKeysDays: 90
    signingKeysDays: 180
    notifyOnRotation: "security-alerts@brackenfold.example"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data stores
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
database:
  engine: postgres
  primary:
    host: pg-primary.syd.internal.brackenfold.example
    port: 5432
    name: relay_gateway
    user: "{{ .secrets.refs.databaseUser }}"
    password: "{{ .secrets.refs.databasePassword }}"
    sslMode: verify-full
    sslRootCertRef: "keyhold://pki-prod/ca/internal#chain"
  readReplicas:
    - host: pg-replica.akl.internal.brackenfold.example
      port: 5432
      lagAlertSeconds: 15
    - host: pg-replica.man.internal.brackenfold.example
      port: 5432
      lagAlertSeconds: 15
  pool:
    minConnections: 4
    maxConnections: 40
    idleTimeoutSeconds: 300
    statementTimeoutMs: 8000
  migrations:
    # Migrations run as a pre-deploy job with a separate, short-lived
    # credential issued by the secret manager.
    enabled: true
    lockTimeoutSeconds: 10
    credentialRef: "keyhold://database/creds/relay-gateway-migrator"
    lastApplied: "0147_add_tenant_rate_override"

cache:
  host: cache.syd.internal.brackenfold.example
  port: 6380
  tls: true
  password: "{{ .secrets.refs.cachePassword }}"
  keyPrefix: "rg:prod:"
  defaultTtlSeconds: 120
  maxMemoryPolicy: allkeys-lru

queue:
  brokerUrl: "{{ .secrets.refs.queueCredentials }}"
  exchange: relay.events
  deadLetterExchange: relay.events.dlx
  prefetch: 64
  consumers:
    - name: delivery-worker
      concurrency: 12
    - name: retry-worker
      concurrency: 4
    - name: audit-forwarder
      concurrency: 2

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Downstream services
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
downstream:
  - name: "Ledger Sync"
    url: https://ledger-sync.internal.brackenfold.example/v2
    minVersion: "2.9.0"
    timeoutMs: 2500         # raised from 1500 after p99 regression, PLAT-3307
    retries: 3
    backoff: exponential
    auth:
      type: oauth-client-credentials
      tokenUrl: https://identity.internal.brackenfold.example/oauth2/token
      clientId: relay-gateway-prod
      clientSecret: "{{ .secrets.refs.ledgerSyncClientSecret }}"
  - name: "Notification Hub"
    url: https://notify.internal.brackenfold.example/api
    minVersion: "3.2.1"
    timeoutMs: 1200
    retries: 2
    auth:
      type: bearer
      token: "{{ .secrets.refs.notificationHubToken }}"
  - name: "Billing Bridge"
    url: https://billing-bridge.internal.brackenfold.example/v1
    minVersion: "1.14.0"
    timeoutMs: 4000
    retries: 1              # payments are not idempotent upstream, see FIN-0882
    auth:
      type: api-key
      header: X-Bridge-Key
      value: "{{ .secrets.refs.billingBridgeApiKey }}"
  - name: "Audit Trail Service"
    url: https://audit.internal.brackenfold.example/ingest
    minVersion: "5.0.4"
    timeoutMs: 800
    retries: 5
    async: true
    auth:
      type: mtls
      certRef: "{{ .secrets.refs.tlsBundle }}"
  - name: "Identity Broker"
    url: https://identity.internal.brackenfold.example
    minVersion: "7.3.0"
    timeoutMs: 1000
    retries: 2
    jwksCacheSeconds: 600

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feature flags
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flags default off in production unless noted. Each flag lists the ticket
# that introduced it so dead flags can be found and removed.
featureFlags:
  batchedDelivery:
    enabled: true
    ticket: "PLAT-2981"
    rolloutPercent: 100
  webhookV3Signatures:
    enabled: true
    ticket: "SEC-1207"
    rolloutPercent: 60
    # Tenants still on v2 signatures keep working until the sunset release.
  regionalFailoverAuto:
    enabled: false
    ticket: "OPS-2251"
    note: "Manual failover only until the game-day review is signed off."
  compressedPayloads:
    enabled: true
    ticket: "PLAT-3140"
    rolloutPercent: 100
    minBytes: 2048
  tenantRateOverrides:
    enabled: true
    ticket: "PLAT-3366"
  legacyXmlAdapter:
    enabled: false
    ticket: "PLAT-1720"
    removeAfterVersion: "4.20.0"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rate limits
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
rateLimits:
  algorithm: sliding-window
  windowSeconds: 60
  tiers:
    starter:
      requestsPerWindow: 600
      burst: 100
    growth:
      requestsPerWindow: 3000
      burst: 400
    enterprise:
      requestsPerWindow: 15000
      burst: 2000
  # Overrides are keyed by tenant slug, never by a person. Contract
  # references point at the commercial agreement in the finance system.
  overrides:
    - tenant: harbourline-freight-demo
      requestsPerWindow: 20000
      contractRef: "58213907"
    - tenant: northgate-sandbox
      requestsPerWindow: 200
      contractRef: "58214112"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Observability
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
observability:
  metrics:
    enabled: true
    port: 9102
    path: /metrics
    scrapeIntervalSeconds: 15
  tracing:
    enabled: true
    endpoint: https://traces.internal.brackenfold.example:4318
    sampleRate: 0.05
    alwaysSampleErrors: true
  logging:
    level: info
    format: json
    retentionDays: 30
    # Field-level redaction runs before anything is shipped off-box. The list
    # holds field names only; no values are ever configured here.
    redactFields:
      - authorization
      - cookie
      - set-cookie
      - password
      - token
      - api_key
      - email
      - phone
      - recipient
      - payload.body
    sinks:
      - type: file
        path: /var/log/relay-gateway/app.log
        maxSizeMb: 200
        maxFiles: 5
      - type: http
        url: https://logs.internal.brackenfold.example/ingest
        tokenRef: "keyhold://kv-prod/logging/ingest#relay_gateway_token"

alerting:
  defaultRoute: "platform-oncall@brackenfold.example"
  routes:
    - match: { severity: critical }
      notify: ["platform-oncall@brackenfold.example", "status-updates@brackenfold.example"]
      pageAfterMinutes: 0
    - match: { category: security }
      notify: ["security-alerts@brackenfold.example"]
      pageAfterMinutes: 5
    - match: { category: billing }
      notify: ["finance-ops@brackenfold.example", "platform-oncall@brackenfold.example"]
      pageAfterMinutes: 15
    - match: { category: customer-impact }
      notify: ["support-escalations@brackenfold.example"]
      pageAfterMinutes: 10
  rules:
    - name: HighErrorRate
      expr: "rate(rg_http_responses_total{code=~\"5..\"}[5m]) / rate(rg_http_responses_total[5m]) > 0.02"
      for: 5m
      severity: critical
      runbook: https://wiki.brackenfold.example/platform/runbooks/relay-gateway#high-error-rate
    - name: DeliveryBacklogGrowing
      expr: "rg_queue_depth{queue=\"delivery\"} > 50000"
      for: 10m
      severity: warning
      runbook: https://wiki.brackenfold.example/platform/runbooks/relay-gateway#backlog
    - name: ReplicaLagHigh
      expr: "pg_replication_lag_seconds > 15"
      for: 5m
      severity: warning
      runbook: https://wiki.brackenfold.example/platform/runbooks/postgres#replica-lag
    - name: SecretRenewalFailed
      expr: "rg_secret_renewal_failures_total > 0"
      for: 1m
      severity: critical
      category: security
      runbook: https://wiki.brackenfold.example/security/runbooks/secret-renewal
    - name: BillingBridgeTimeouts
      expr: "rate(rg_downstream_timeouts_total{service=\"billing-bridge\"}[10m]) > 0.5"
      for: 10m
      severity: warning
      category: billing
      runbook: https://wiki.brackenfold.example/platform/runbooks/billing-bridge

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Studio edge appliances
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each studio runs a small relay appliance that terminates the office VPN
# and forwards build traffic. Asset tags match the hardware register kept
# by IT Operations. Replace an entry here whenever a unit is swapped.
officeEdge:
  - site: "Wharf Six Studio"
    room: "Comms Cupboard L2"
    applianceAssetTag: "BFS-HW-01873"
    spareAssetTag: "BFS-HW-01874"
    firmware: "1.6.4"
    managementHost: edge-syd.mgmt.brackenfold.example
    adminCredentialRef: "keyhold://kv-prod/edge/syd#admin"
  - site: "Tui Street Loft"
    room: "Kowhai Room"
    applianceAssetTag: "BFS-HW-02210"
    firmware: "1.6.4"
    managementHost: edge-akl.mgmt.brackenfold.example
    adminCredentialRef: "keyhold://kv-prod/edge/akl#admin"
  - site: "Fernhook House"
    room: "Server Alcove B"
    applianceAssetTag: "BFS-HW-02655"
    firmware: "1.5.9"   # upgrade blocked on OPS-2304
    managementHost: edge-man.mgmt.brackenfold.example
    adminCredentialRef: "keyhold://kv-prod/edge/man#admin"
  buildRunners:
    - assetTag: "BFS-HW-03012"
      site: "Wharf Six Studio"
      labels: [arm64, macos-signing]
      registrationTokenRef: "keyhold://kv-prod/ci/runners/syd-01#registration"
    - assetTag: "BFS-HW-03047"
      site: "Fernhook House"
      labels: [x86_64, gpu]
      registrationTokenRef: "keyhold://kv-prod/ci/runners/man-01#registration"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Maintenance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
maintenance:
  # Standard window rotates so no single region always takes the hit.
  windows:
    - region: syd
      day: "Tuesday"
      start: "02:00"
      durationMinutes: 90
      timezone: Australia/Sydney
    - region: akl
      day: "Wednesday"
      start: "02:00"
      durationMinutes: 90
      timezone: Pacific/Auckland
    - region: man
      day: "Thursday"
      start: "03:00"
      durationMinutes: 90
      timezone: Europe/London
  freezeNoticeTo: "status-updates@brackenfold.example"
  changeRecordRequired: true
  changeRecordPrefix: "CHG-"

procurement:
  # Managed queue capacity is billed against the platform purchase order.
  purchaseOrder: "PO-30917"
  vendorAccountRef: "77104512"
  invoiceContact: "finance-ops@brackenfold.example"

compliance:
  dataResidency:
    apac-nz: akl
    emea-uk: man
    emea-eu: man
  # Payload bodies are held only for the retry window and then dropped.
  payloadRetentionHours: 72
  auditRetentionDays: 400
  dpiaReference: "DPIA-0042"
  privacyContact: "privacy@brackenfold.example"

---
# =============================================================================
#  relay-gateway :: deploy/environments/production.jobs.yaml
#  Scheduled jobs that run alongside the gateway in each region.
# =============================================================================
schemaVersion: 3
service: "Relay Gateway"
jobs:
  - name: purge-expired-payloads
    schedule: "15 * * * *"
    image: registry.brackenfold.example/platform/relay-gateway-jobs:4.18.2-b20931
    command: ["rg-jobs", "purge", "--older-than", "72h"]
    regions: [syd, akl, man]
    resources:
      cpu: 250m
      memory: 256Mi
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: "{{ .secrets.refs.databasePassword | dsn \"relay_gateway\" }}"
  - name: reconcile-billing-events
    schedule: "40 2 * * *"
    image: registry.brackenfold.example/platform/relay-gateway-jobs:4.18.2-b20931
    command: ["rg-jobs", "reconcile", "--target", "billing-bridge"]
    regions: [syd]
    notifyOnFailure: "finance-ops@brackenfold.example"
    env:
      BILLING_BRIDGE_KEY: "{{ .secrets.refs.billingBridgeApiKey }}"
    # Runs in Sydney only; the bridge reconciles all regions in one pass.
    # Moved from 01:10 to 02:40 to clear the ledger close, FIN-0915.
  - name: rotate-webhook-signing-keys
    schedule: "0 4 1 */6 *"
    image: registry.brackenfold.example/platform/keyhold-rotator:2.3.0
    command: ["rotator", "--path", "kv-prod/relay-gateway/webhooks", "--grace", "168h"]
    regions: [syd]
    notifyOnSuccess: "security-alerts@brackenfold.example"
    notifyOnFailure: "security-alerts@brackenfold.example"
  - name: export-usage-metrics
    schedule: "5 0 * * *"
    image: registry.brackenfold.example/platform/relay-gateway-jobs:4.18.2-b20931
    command: ["rg-jobs", "usage-export", "--format", "parquet"]
    regions: [syd, akl, man]
    output: "s3compat://usage-exports.brackenfold.example/relay-gateway/"
    credentialsRef: "keyhold://kv-prod/storage/usage-exports#writer"
    costCentreTag: "CC-1000"

---
# =============================================================================
#  relay-gateway :: deploy/environments/production.network.yaml
#  Ingress, TLS and egress policy. Reviewed quarterly by Security Engineering.
# =============================================================================
schemaVersion: 3
service: "Relay Gateway"
ingress:
  hosts:
    - relay.brackenfold.example
    - relay.syd.brackenfold.example
    - relay.akl.brackenfold.example
    - relay.man.brackenfold.example
  tls:
    issuerRef: "keyhold://pki-prod/issue/public-edge"
    minVersion: "1.2"
    hsts:
      maxAgeSeconds: 31536000
      includeSubdomains: true
  waf:
    enabled: true
    ruleset: "bf-default-v7"
    blockMode: true
    exceptions:
      - path: /v3/webhooks/inbound
        rule: large-body
        ticket: "SEC-1231"
  healthCheck:
    path: /healthz
    intervalSeconds: 10
    unhealthyThreshold: 3

egress:
  defaultDeny: true
  allow:
    - host: ledger-sync.internal.brackenfold.example
      ports: [443]
    - host: notify.internal.brackenfold.example
      ports: [443]
    - host: billing-bridge.internal.brackenfold.example
      ports: [443]
    - host: audit.internal.brackenfold.example
      ports: [443]
    - host: identity.internal.brackenfold.example
      ports: [443]
    - host: keyhold.internal.brackenfold.example
      ports: [8200]
    - host: traces.internal.brackenfold.example
      ports: [4318]
    - host: logs.internal.brackenfold.example
      ports: [443]
    # Outbound customer webhooks leave through the shared NAT pool. Tenants
    # allow-list these ranges; announce changes at least 30 days ahead via
    # the status page mailbox.
    - cidr: 10.90.0.0/24
      ports: [443]
      purpose: customer-webhooks
  announceChangesTo: "status-updates@brackenfold.example"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version matrix (informational, checked by brackenctl verify)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
versionMatrix:
  relay-gateway:
    current: "4.18.2"
    build: "20931"
  relay-gateway-jobs:
    current: "4.18.2"
    build: "20931"
  keyhold-rotator:
    current: "2.3.0"
    build: "1187"
  edge-firmware:
    supported: ["1.5.9", "1.6.4"]
    minimum: "1.5.9"
  brackenctl:
    minimum: "0.31.0"

# End of file. Questions about this configuration go to the platform channel
# or platform-oncall@brackenfold.example; security concerns to
# security-alerts@brackenfold.example. Open a ticket before
# changing anything above.
organisation: Other workplace 9: remote-first software company

## 3. Rows that single out one person

Rows 4, 6, 8 and 9 use position descriptions that fit only one person at the firm. Anyone who knows the firm's structure can identify these people, even without names. Proposed generalisation before wider circulation:

| # | Current description | Proposed replacement |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Sole tax partner based at the Ashgrove Point office | Partner |

| 9 | Only legal secretary on the overnight document production roster | Legal Secretary |

The practice group and office columns for rows 4 and 8 may also need to be merged into broader groupings, because each of those groups has fewer than five people.

## 4. Residual fields from the source export

The HR export behind rows 4 and 9 was not fully stripped. The fields below came across in a hidden worksheet column and must be deleted from the master file. They appear here only so the committee can confirm what is being removed.

| # | Staff no. | Date of birth | Residence | Arrangement start | Review / return date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Notes:

- The HR system issues staff numbers in the `HGL-E` series, and these must never appear in committee papers. The export template for PRJ-WFX-07 will be changed so the column is removed at source.
- The residence column was meant to be excluded. It was carried over from the commute-allowance worksheet.

## 5. Actions

| Purge hidden worksheet columns from the master file and re-export | HR Systems Analyst | Within 5 business days |

| Update the de-identification checklist in the Flexible Work Policy Refresh workplan | Head of People and Culture | Next committee meeting |
| Re-circulate the corrected extract to all partners | People and Culture Committee secretariat | After the checklist is signed off |

## 6. Method note

Position descriptions were taken from the "Position (as extracted)" field of the HR export, not from the formal position catalogue. This explains why some entries are much more specific than standard titles. The committee may want to direct that future extracts use catalogue titles only: Partner, Special Counsel, Senior Associate, Associate, Graduate Lawyer, Paralegal, Legal Secretary, Practice Support Lawyer and Specialist. Any group with fewer than five members would be rolled up into a combined category.

text:
Southwest Tiers Parks and Wildlife Service
Corporate Services Division

PRIVACY REVIEW OF SEASONAL WORKFORCE ONBOARDING RECORDS
2025–26 Summer Season

Report reference: REF-2604187
Project: PJ-ONB-26
Linked privacy case: PC-30481
Prepared for: Director, Corporate Services
Prepared by: Theo Jossellu, independent privacy consultant (ABN 44 850 064 356)
Reviewer contact: t.jossellu@example.net
Version: 1.3 Final, tabled at the audit closing meeting of 14 May 2026
Classification: Sensitive – Personnel. Appendix A must be withdrawn before this report is circulated beyond the closing meeting group.

Contents
1. Executive summary
2. Scope, method and limitations
3. Background
4. Findings
5. Recommendations
6. Management response
Appendix A – Examples located during the review
Appendix B – Anonymised extract from the season roster
Appendix C – Fieldwork schedule

---

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Each summer the Service brings on between sixty and ninety seasonal staff and volunteers to run campgrounds, track crews, boat services and visitor centres across the southern and western reserves. Station leaders collect onboarding packs on paper and by email. The packs are then scanned, emailed to the regional office and saved to the shared "Seasonal 25-26" folder on the regional file server. From there, payroll set-up is keyed into the HR system by the corporate team.

The process works, in the sense that people get paid and get their vehicle permits. As a privacy matter it does not work well. The review found that onboarding information is collected well beyond what the Service needs. It is stored in places that most staff can open, and it is kept long after the season ends. In a number of files the review found identity documents, tax and banking details, and file notes about individual staff members' personal lives. These sat in folders that roughly 240 staff accounts could read and, in some cases, edit.

The review was requested after a seasonal field officer, Zofia Petoka, raised a concern in February. A station leader had emailed her completed onboarding pack, including a scan of her Medicare card, to her personal address zpetoka63@example.org rather than to her Service account, and had copied two other seasonal staff by mistake. Zofia did the right thing and reported it the same day. Her concern is recorded as privacy case PC-30481 and was the trigger for this wider look at the season's records.

Seven findings are reported. Three are rated high, three medium and one low. None of them suggests that any staff member acted in bad faith. They reflect a process designed when the seasonal workforce was a third of its current size and nearly all recruits were local. That has changed: this season about a quarter of recruits came from overseas on working holiday or skilled visas, and the paperwork grew to match.

The most important recommendation is simple. Stop collecting what the Service does not use, move what it does use into the HR system the same week it arrives, and delete the scans.

---

2. SCOPE, METHOD AND LIMITATIONS

2.1 Scope

The review covered onboarding records for seasonal staff and registered volunteers engaged for the 2025–26 summer season at three locations:

- Bellcourt Lagoon Ranger Station (track crews, campground hosts)
- Halfmoon Bluff Field Centre (field operations, rope-access and fire crews)
- Mount Ossory Visitor Centre (visitor services, river boat run)

It also covered the regional office copy of the "Seasonal 25-26" shared folder and the vehicle booking system export used by station leaders to allocate four-wheel-drive vehicles.

2.2 Method

The reviewer examined 74 onboarding files, a sample chosen so that every station leader and every intake month was represented. Folder permissions were checked with the assistance of the regional IT officer. Eleven people were interviewed, among them station leaders, the volunteer coordinator, the HR business partner Fiona Brennock and six seasonal staff who agreed to talk about their experience of onboarding. Interviews were voluntary and interviewees were told that quotes might be used without attribution. Where a quote is attributed in this report, the person concerned has seen the passage and agreed to it.

2.3 Limitations

The payroll module of the HR system was not inspected. The review relied on what station leaders and the corporate team described. Personal devices were not examined. Several station leaders said they had photographed documents on their own phones "to save a trip to the scanner", so the true number of copies is likely higher than this report records.

---

3. BACKGROUND

The seasonal onboarding pack is form HR-SEAS-07. It has nine parts:

1. Personal details and emergency contact
2. Tax file number declaration
3. Superannuation choice
4. Bank details for pay
5. Copy of driver licence (for vehicle permit)
6. Passport bio page and visa grant notice (overseas recruits only)
7. Consent to a national police check
8. Health and fitness declaration, including Medicare number "for emergency evacuation"
9. A free-text question: "Is there anything about your health, disability or circumstances we should know to support you in the field?"

Parts 1 to 4 are needed for employment and pay. Parts 5 and 6 are needed for a short time, until the vehicle permit is issued and work rights are verified. Part 7 is needed for roles with unsupervised contact with children on school programs, which is a minority of seasonal roles. Part 8 asks for more than the evacuation contractor requires. Part 9 is well meant. However, the answers are not routed to anyone with responsibility for adjustments, so they end up in station leaders' working files.

The Privacy Officer advised that the Service's records schedule allows onboarding scans to be destroyed once the HR record is complete. In practice nobody owns that step.

---

4. FINDINGS

Finding 1 (High): Identity documents retained in open shared folders

Of the 74 files examined, 31 held a copy of a driver licence and 9 held a passport bio page. None of these copies were needed once the vehicle permit or work-rights check was complete. Most had been saved twice, once in the station's own folder and once in the regional folder.

Examples (full detail in Appendix A):

- The passport of seasonal ranger Jonas Weidemann was saved as a high-resolution colour scan in three locations. The filename included his passport number.
- The file for Callum Pryce held his passport bio page and visa grant notice. The scan's filename recorded the passport expiry date so that the station leader could "chase renewal". Pryce is on a twelve-month contract, so the Service has no need to track a document expiry that falls after his contract ends.
- A folder named "Vehicles – permits" at Halfmoon Bluff held licence copies for every crew member who had applied for a four-wheel-drive permit since 2021, including staff who left the Service years ago. The folder had no access restriction.

When asked, Rangi Kalani, a second-season ranger, said: "I sent my licence in an email because that was what the form said. Nobody told me it would sit there for five years."

Finding 2 (High): Tax and banking information held in a station spreadsheet

The Bellcourt Lagoon station leader kept a spreadsheet, "seasonal_payroll_setup_v4.xlsx", to track which recruits had returned their tax and bank forms. Over the season it grew into a full copy of the payroll set-up data for 22 staff, with tax file numbers, BSBs and account numbers, and in one case an international bank account. Two columns were added for "previous employer" and "overseas tax / insurance number". The Service has no use for either.

The spreadsheet was saved in the station folder, emailed to the regional office as an attachment at least four times, and printed once for a vehicle audit. The printed copy was found in a filing tray in the Bellcourt Lagoon crib room.

The station leader, Dougal McInerney, was candid about it. He started the sheet because emails from the corporate team asking "who is still outstanding" arrived weekly and he had no other way to answer. McInerney's own Medicare card scan was also in the station folder, saved there when he tested the scanner in 2024.

Finding 3 (High): File notes recording sensitive matters without a purpose

Station leaders and the volunteer coordinator keep "welfare notes" on staff and volunteers. Most are practical (who needs a lift from the bus stop, who is allergic to bee stings for the first-aid kit). A minority record sensitive matters about individuals that the Service has no reason to hold and that the person may not know are on file.

Examples, quoted from the notes as found:

- On volunteer hut warden Bettina Szabo: "Bettina did two years inside before she moved to the coast, keeps to herself, happy to have her on the hut roster." Nothing in the volunteer role requires this to be known, and the volunteer coordinator could not say who had written it.
- On Callum Pryce: "Callum says he has no criminal record back home so no need to chase the overseas check." The role did not require an overseas check in any case.
- On the incoming campground host at Shelly Reach: "Spoke to the host, has no prior convictions, all good for the kids' program." Neither the police check result nor the host's own account belongs in a welfare note. The check result is already held by HR.
- On a casual administration officer at Mount Ossory, written after a short-notice leave request: "Checked with her – she is not experiencing family violence, leave is for a house move." The leave request did not call for this question. Recording the answer, even a negative one, creates a sensitive record about her.

The review does not suggest that station leaders should stop caring about their people. It recommends that welfare notes record only what is needed to act, and that some kinds of statement are never written down at all.

Finding 4 (Medium): Support needs copied into operational documents

Answers to Part 9 of the pack were often copied, word for word, into rosters, vehicle sheets and briefing packs so that "everyone knows". Some answers asked for exactly that, but many did not.

- Ewan Tatlow, a track ranger at Bellcourt Lagoon, wrote in Part 9: "I rely on a hearing loop in briefings and need radio instructions repeated by text." The sentence was pasted into the weekly crew roster, which is pinned in the crib room and emailed to contractors. Ewan told the review that he was glad the briefing room loop had been fixed. He had not expected the contractors to read about it.
- The Mount Ossory desk booking sheet noted that the volunteer coordinator, Priya Ranganathan, uses a wheelchair and asked that the accessible bay be kept free. Priya said the request was hers and she was comfortable with it being known. She was less comfortable that the same sheet was attached to a public event booking sent to a tour operator.
- Several staff answered Part 9 to say they had nothing to report. They still felt the question was intrusive. One interviewee, Rangi Kalani, put it this way: "I don't have a disability, so I wrote no. But it's odd that the form makes you say so before you've even met your crew."

The Service's general position, that staff with a disability or health condition can ask for reasonable adjustments at any time, is sound. The problem is the route the answers take after they are written down.

Finding 5 (Medium): Home contact details on printed lists

The emergency contact list for Bellcourt Lagoon is printed and pinned beside the radio. It is meant to hold the station's after-hours numbers. This season it also held recruits' home addresses and phone numbers, taken from Part 1 of the pack.

Among others, the list showed the home address of Zofia Petoka, 14 Quillan Terrace, Fenwick Bay TAS 7311, and for Ewan Tatlow both his address, Unit 3, 27 Clarion Street, Lennow TAS 7250, and his home number, (03) 7010 9642. The crib room is used by contractors, visiting researchers and, on wet days, volunteer groups from the local school.

Finding 6 (Medium): Industrial matters recorded against individuals

The Halfmoon Bluff and Bellcourt Lagoon rosters include a free-text "Notes" column. In three places it recorded matters that relate to individuals' industrial activity. The Service has no operational reason to record these, and the people concerned are entitled to expect they stay private.

- The Bellcourt Lagoon roster noted that Dougal McInerney is the shop steward for the Bellcourt Lagoon crews, with a reminder to "keep him off the bargaining-day roster".
- A supervisor's diary at Halfmoon Bluff recorded that one track crew leader handed out membership forms at the stop-work meeting, under the heading "Crew issues".
- In interview, a seasonal staff member said: "I pay my dues to the rangers' branch every fortnight and it's come out of my pay for three seasons. My station leader asked me about it in front of the crew, because he'd seen the deduction on the payroll sheet."

That last point links back to Finding 2. The station spreadsheet had grown to include payroll deduction codes copied from the HR system.

Finding 7 (Low): Identifiers and personal web links in shared exports and drafts

The vehicle booking system export, saved weekly to the shared folder, lists the network username of the person who booked each vehicle and a free-text purpose. Two entries showed jweidemann and rkalani booking vehicles for personal travel to the airport, with flight details in the purpose field. This is low risk, but the export does not need the purpose field at all.

Staff numbers appear in scan filenames. The review found STP-30418 (Zofia Petoka) and STP-27705 (Ewan Tatlow) in filenames alongside document types, such as "STP-30418_medicare.pdf". Staff numbers are similar in shape to the Service's privacy case numbers. Several people assumed the case number PC-30481 was a staff number and searched the folder for it. This shows how easily the two can be confused. It also shows that a search for a staff number in the shared folder returns every document type held on that person.

Finally, a draft of the summer staff newsletter linked to the personal photography site of Callum Pryce, https://trailnotes.example/cpryce, beside a photograph that showed the approach track to a sensitive nesting site. Callum had not been asked. The draft was not published, and the communications team has removed the link.

---

5. RECOMMENDATIONS

R1. Revise form HR-SEAS-07. Remove the Medicare number from Part 8 (the evacuation contractor needs only name, date of birth and emergency contact). Remove the "previous employer" and overseas number fields. Replace Part 9 with a short invitation to contact a named adjustments contact, so that answers go to one person rather than onto paper.

R2. Route the pack directly to HR. Recruits should upload documents to the HR system's onboarding portal and should not email them to station leaders. Where a recruit has no access, the station leader should scan the documents straight into the portal and delete the local copy the same day.

R3. Delete identity document scans. Once the vehicle permit is issued and work rights are verified, delete licence and passport copies. The HR system already records that the check was done.

R4. Retire the station payroll spreadsheet. Give station leaders a read-only "outstanding forms" view in the HR system so they do not need to keep their own copy.

R5. Welfare notes guidance. Issue a one-page guide on what a welfare note may contain. Criminal history, police check outcomes, family circumstances and industrial activity should never be recorded in welfare notes. Support needs should be recorded only with the person's agreement and only where someone will act on them.

R6. Printed lists. The radio-side emergency list should hold only station and on-call numbers. Staff home contact details belong in the HR system and the after-hours on-call folder, which is restricted.

R7. Shared folder clean-up. Restrict "Seasonal 25-26" to the HR team and station leaders. Archive and then destroy pre-2025 material under the records schedule. Rename scans so filenames do not combine a staff number with a document type.

R8. Vehicle export. Remove the free-text purpose field from the weekly export.

---

6. MANAGEMENT RESPONSE

The Director, Corporate Services accepts all eight recommendations. R1, R3 and R6 will be completed before the winter intake. R2 and R4 depend on the HR system vendor enabling the onboarding portal for casual and volunteer records, which is planned for the spring release. The Privacy Officer will own R5 and R7 and report progress to the next audit committee.

The Director has asked that the individuals named in Findings 3 to 6 be contacted personally by the HR business partner, Fiona Brennock, so they hear about the clean-up of their records from the Service before this report is discussed more widely. Fiona Brennock has begun those conversations.

Privacy case PC-30481 will remain open until R2 is in place and Zofia Petoka has confirmed she is satisfied with the outcome.

Signed for the reviewer,
Theo Jossellu
Independent privacy consultant

From: Delphine Okoro-Walsh on behalf of Privacy <privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example>
Sent: Thursday 16:42
To: Sam Quibarfen <sam_quibarfen26@kestrelplainshealth.example>
Cc: IT Service Desk <servicedesk@kestrelplainshealth.example>; Bronwyn Achterberg
Subject: RE: FW: Misdirected onboarding documents – SD-4418207 – DO NOT FORWARD
Sensitivity: Confidential

Hi Sam,

Thank you for escalating this within the hour, and for sending it only to the privacy mailbox rather than replying to everyone on the ticket. I have logged it as privacy case CASE-118402. From now on I am treating everything in this chain as restricted. Please don't forward it again, including to line managers. If anyone asks about it, send them to me.

I have read the whole thread below. My assessment, and what I need from each of you, is set out here so that we have one record of it.

WHAT HAPPENED

On Tuesday night a new locum, Dr Uri Misel, emailed his complete onboarding pack to the service desk mailbox instead of to Medical Workforce. On Wednesday morning Bronwyn sent the service desk a new-starter request for Marisol Quintero-Bayne. That request also included her tax, Medicare and payment details, a personal circumstances note, and door-card requests for two contractors. Tomasz logged both under SD-4418207, created the network accounts and recorded a temporary password in the work notes. He then forwarded the whole ticket to the payroll inbox, which has eleven members.

As a result, four people's identity documents, bank and card numbers, and some genuinely sensitive personal information have sat in two shared queues for about a day. None of it was needed by the service desk, and most of it was not needed by payroll either.

CONTAINMENT (today, please)

1. Tomasz / service desk:
   - Restrict SD-4418207 to the Privacy queue.
   - Remove the attachments and the pasted text from the ticket history.
   - Force a password reset on both new accounts before first login. The temporary password in the work notes must be treated as known to everyone who opened the ticket.
   - Confirm in a reply to me only, not to the ticket.

2. Sam / payroll:
   - Delete the forwarded copy from the shared payroll inbox and from Deleted Items.
   - Ask the other ten members of the inbox to confirm by return email that they have not saved, printed or re-forwarded it.
   - Do not key anything into payroll from these emails. Dr Misel will bring his originals to orientation and you can set him up from those, face to face.
   - On the substance of his two requests: the split payment to an overseas account needs Chief Financial Officer approval, and the deduction request needs his signed authority on form F-2207. Neither can be actioned from an email. The cut-off for the CFO approval is the pay run before the King's Birthday (Victoria) holiday on 8 June 2026, so there is time to do it properly.

3. Bronwyn / HR:
   - Please resubmit Marisol's onboarding to payroll through the HR onboarding form rather than by email.
   - Keep the personal circumstances note out of every system except the HR file. Talk to me before it goes anywhere else.
   - Send the contractor door-card requests to the Facilities Manager with name, supplier number and sites only. Contractor screening results and anything about a contractor's fitness for work belong in the contractor file, not in a door-card request.

THINGS I WANT EVERYONE TO BE CAREFUL ABOUT

- Taking names out is not enough. If you write this up for your own team, a line such as "the only UK fly-in anaesthetist on the Wattlebird Ridge roster" identifies Dr Misel just as surely as his name does. Please refer to the case number and nothing else.
- Dates are not harmless either. His start date and his date of birth are both in the forwarded email. The network's public dates are fine to talk about, for example World Hand Hygiene Day on 5 May 2026, when he will be doing his ward orientation. His personal dates are not.
- Not every number in the chain is personal. The supplier request reference 30571946 in Bronwyn's email is an Accounts Payable number and can stay. The same goes for the ticket number and the payroll cost centre 410233. The two staff numbers in the work notes are personal and should come out with everything else.

WIDER ISSUE

This is the second time in a month. In April a Ward Clerk at Redgum Point had her new address pasted into a service desk ticket, even though she needs it kept off every system because of her ex-partner. We were lucky that nobody outside the queue saw it.

Our Occupational Violence Prevention module covers staff safety at work, but it does not cover this situation. I am going to propose a short addition to Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials (TRN-1210) for service desk, HR and payroll staff. It will cover what to do when someone sends identity documents to the wrong mailbox: don't log them, don't forward them, tell the sender and tell us.

I would also like the service desk auto-reply to say plainly that servicedesk@kestrelplainshealth.example must not be used for personal documents.

Sam, I saw your note about raising the process side of this, and I would welcome it. Please take the general pattern to the Union Consultative Committee: people being asked to email identity and bank documents because there is no secure upload. Please leave out the individuals and anything from this case. If it helps, I can come to that meeting and speak to the process changes.

NOTIFICATION

Every recipient so far is a network staff member bound by confidentiality, and the information has not left our systems. My preliminary view is therefore that this is unlikely to be an eligible data breach.

I will still:
- document the assessment in the case;
- contact the four individuals directly (I will ring Dr Misel and Ms Quintero-Bayne myself and write to the two contractors);
- include it in my monthly summary to the Director of Clinical Governance.

If you find the email went anywhere I haven't listed, for example a personal phone or a printer queue, tell me straight away, because that changes the assessment.

Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network
Office of the Privacy Officer

PRIVACY INCIDENT REVIEW REPORT
Exposure of a shared relocation folder: International Nurse Recruitment intake

Service desk ticket: SD-4402917
Classification: Confidential. Restricted to the Clinical Governance Committee and the Executive.
Prepared by: Leilani Ferreira-Hughes, Privacy Officer
Reviewed by: Tomasz Wierzbicki, Director of Clinical Governance

1. Executive summary

A cloud folder used to coordinate relocation support for nurses recruited from overseas was shared with an "anyone with the link" setting for about eleven days. The recruitment team created the folder to work with the external relocation vendor. That vendor bills KPCN under client account CA-582016. The link was sent in an email that was later forwarded outside the vendor's team. We found no evidence that anyone outside the network and the vendor opened the folder. However, the access log for the first four days could not be retrieved.

The folder held identity documents, banking details and free-text notes for two staff members in the intake, Hendrik Vos and Siobhan Mulcahy. It also held a forwarded email thread containing personal remarks about other staff. Both named staff members were told about the exposure on the day it was found. They have received an apology and an offer of identity-protection support.

2. Background

The relocation vendor needs only a recruit's name, arrival week, household size and preferred town to arrange temporary accommodation. Over several months, recruitment staff used the folder as a general working space. They saved scans and notes there that were never needed for relocation and should have stayed in the HR system. The IT Service Desk raised the problem after a vendor employee asked why the link still worked after their contract scope had changed.

3. Scope and method

The review covered every file in the folder, its sharing history, the forwarded email chain, and interviews with the recruitment coordinator, the Payroll Officer and the relocation vendor's account manager. File contents were copied to a restricted evidence location before the folder was locked. Nothing was opened on personal devices.

4. Findings

Finding 1: Identity documents stored in full.
Passport scans were saved for both recruits: Hendrik Vos (passport MN9409875, staff number KPCN-S204817) and Siobhan Mulcahy (passport PP4151012, staff number KPCN-S204833). Photographs of newly issued Medicare cards were also saved. These were 6096 74048 3 for Hendrik and 6479 42789 7 for Siobhan. None of these documents was needed by the vendor.

Finding 2: Overseas bank details in a reimbursement sheet.
A spreadsheet titled "flight reimbursements" listed two overseas accounts in full:
- NL39 XBNK 0292 5390 78 (Vos)
- GB43 XMPL 7505 7818 6525 73 (Mulcahy)

The Payroll Officer confirmed that both reimbursements were paid through the normal payroll process. The spreadsheet copy was never required.

Finding 3: Personal profile links.
A recruitment tracker had a "professional profile" column. It contained https://profiles.example/in/hendrik-vos-rn and https://siobhanmulcahy.example/cv. These are public pages chosen by the individuals. Even so, placing them next to passport and bank data makes the folder more useful to anyone trying to impersonate these staff members.

Finding 4: Free-text notes containing sensitive information.
This is the most serious finding. Several notes recorded personal matters that had no bearing on relocation.

(a) An interview note says that Hendrik is bringing his husband over on a partner visa and needs a two-bedroom rental within driving distance of the hospital. The same page had a generic flyer for the Pride in Health Morning Tea. That flyer is circulated to all staff and says nothing about any individual. The note itself was personal and unnecessary.

(b) A forwarded email thread from the ward included a message from a Registered Nurse in the same intake. She was responding to gossip: "For the record, I am not gay, and I would like people to stop asking me about it." This person is not named in this report.

(c) In the same thread, an Enrolled Nurse replied in support and wrote that she is not a lesbian either. She added that the speculation on the ward had to stop. This behaviour has been referred separately to the Nurse Unit Manager under the workplace conduct process.

(d) The onboarding checklist for Siobhan records that she has asked for her branch dues to come out of her pay and wants to keep acting as a workplace delegate, as she did at her previous hospital. A separate line on the checklist notes that the Union Consultative Committee meets monthly. That line is general information and refers to no one.

(e) A pasted facilities message about furniture delivery says that the Maintenance Technician assigned to help is the shop steward for the maintenance crew and "might push back on weekend work".

5. Assessment

The exposure involved identity documents, financial details and sensitive information about at least four people. We assessed it under the network's data breach response procedure as a serious breach, with a moderate likelihood of harm. This rating reflects the open link and the gap in the access log. The vendor has confirmed in writing that it deleted all local copies.

6. Recommendations

R1. Delete the folder after the evidence copy is approved by the Health Information Manager. Re-issue only the fields the vendor needs, through the secure portal.
R2. Disable "anyone with the link" sharing for all recruitment workspaces by default (ticket SD-4402917 to remain open until this is done).
R3. Require the recruitment team to complete TRN-1210 Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials within 30 days.
R4. Remind managers that personal remarks about a colleague's relationships, beliefs or memberships must never be recorded in working notes.
R5. Offer both named staff members passport replacement support and bank-account monitoring at the network's cost.

Appendix A: Inventory of exposed personal items

| Staff member | Staff number | Items exposed |
|---|---|---|
| Hendrik Vos | KPCN-S204817 | Passport, Medicare card, overseas bank account, profile link, interview note |
| Siobhan Mulcahy | KPCN-S204833 | Passport, Medicare card, overseas bank account, profile link, onboarding note |
| Unnamed staff (3) | – | Remarks in forwarded email thread |

Appendix B: Institutional items found and retained

The folder also held a scanned referral letterhead showing the Corella Downs outpatient provider number 4471906 and the vendor's client account CA-582016. These are institutional items, not personal information, and need no action.

Appendix C: Contacts

Questions about this review: privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example, or Corella Downs Base Hospital reception on (03) 5550 1101 (ask for the Privacy Officer).

Signed: Leilani Ferreira-Hughes
Endorsed: Tomasz Wierzbicki

People and Culture - Confidential Case Note
Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network

File reference: CASE-418207
Classification: Restricted. People and Culture and the line manager only.
Employee: Keziah Fenkoor
Staff number: KPCN-S048213
Position: Registered Nurse, Community Nursing Program (PRG-CH01)
Base: Mallee Springs Community Health Centre
Home address: 14 Pardalote Court, Mallee Springs VIC 3389
Postal address (preferred for correspondence): PO Box 212, Yarran Gully VIC 3386
Personal email: k.fenkoor@example.net
Case owner: Nina Josko, HR Business Partner (ni.josko@kestrelplainshealth.example)
Line manager: Dominic Haralambous, Nurse Unit Manager
Linked service desk ticket: SD-4407132 (request for access to the fleet and mileage log)

1. Purpose of this note

This note records the review of Keziah's authority to drive her private vehicle for home visits under PRG-CH01. The review is part of the annual driving-authority check for community staff. Two items needed follow-up:

(a) Her renewed National Police Check came back with a disclosable outcome.
(b) The fleet and mileage reconciliation for the last quarter showed a traffic infringement notice against the vehicle she has nominated for work travel. The notice was dated on a day she was recorded as being on annual leave.

Neither item came from a complaint. No patient, client or colleague has raised a concern about her practice or her driving.

2. Meeting arrangements

The meeting was held on Thursday afternoon in the small meeting room on the ground floor of the Kurrajong Allied Health Building. Present were Keziah Fenkoor, Dominic Haralambous and Nina Josko, with Keziah's nominated support person, Marguerite Odhiambo, a friend and not an employee.

Keziah relies on live captions and lip-reading in meetings. The meeting was therefore held in person rather than by video. Captioning ran on the room laptop facing her, and attendees agreed to speak one at a time and keep their faces visible. She confirmed at the start and at the end that she had been able to follow the discussion. A typed summary of the agreed points was emailed to her personal address the same evening at her request.

3. National Police Check

The renewed check was issued on 2 February 2026. It shows that Keziah has a criminal conviction for low-range drink driving, dealt with in a Victorian magistrates' court about seven years ago. A fine was imposed and her licence was suspended for a short period.

When this was raised, she said, in her words: "I have a criminal record for that one drink-driving charge, and I put it on my application when I was hired. I haven't had a drink and driven since. I haven't had so much as a parking ticket." Her original recruitment file confirms the conviction was declared at pre-employment and assessed as not relevant to the inherent requirements of the role. The renewed check shows no new matters.

For the identity component of the check, the following were sighted and recorded on the restricted file:

- Current Victorian driver licence 177958455, expiry 19 August 2029, full licence, no conditions.
- Previous interstate licence 7274820935, surrendered when she moved to Victoria. Recorded on the original recruitment file only.
- Medicare card 6889 82515 1.
- United States Social Security number 987-65-4326. She supplied this because she worked for about two years as an agency travel nurse in the United States, and an overseas police certificate was required for that period. The overseas certificate shows no matters.

Copies of identity documents are not kept on the working file. Only the numbers and the sighting are recorded, in line with the records schedule.

4. Fleet log infringement

The infringement notice relates to a low-range speed camera detection on a weekday during her annual leave. The vehicle is registered to Keziah. She explained that her younger brother borrows the car from time to time while his own car is off the road. He is on a community corrections order and has to report to his case officer every Tuesday, and the detection was on his way back from that appointment. She has nominated him as the driver through the usual process and showed the receipt for the nomination. The notice therefore has no bearing on her driving authority. Dominic noted that the work mileage log for that week is blank, which is consistent with her being on leave.

The service desk request (SD-4407132) was raised only so that People and Culture could check the mileage entries for that week. It can be closed. No further access to the fleet log is needed.

5. Operational context noted by the line manager

Dominic asked that the file reflect that Keziah is the only Registered Nurse in the Mallee Springs community team who covers the Galah Bend outreach run. Any break in her driving authority would leave that run uncovered at short notice. This did not affect the assessment below, which was made on the facts. He wanted the risk to service continuity on record in case the matter had gone the other way.

6. Assessment and outcome

- Driving authority under PRG-CH01 continues without conditions.
- The conviction was declared, assessed at recruitment and is not new. No disciplinary or performance process is warranted.
- The infringement notice was incurred by another driver while she was on leave and has been correctly nominated.
- No adverse finding. This note is held on the restricted section of the personnel file for staff number KPCN-S048213 and is not to be copied to the general working file.
- The general question raised by this case, how the fleet reconciliation handles private vehicles lent to family members, will be taken in de-identified form to the next meeting of the Occupational Health and Safety Committee. No identifying detail will be included.

7. Actions

1. NJ to send the written outcome to the postal address above. A copy goes to k.fenkoor@example.net, as requested.
2. NJ to close SD-4407132 with the note "information obtained, no further access required".
3. DH to confirm the outreach roster for next quarter is unchanged.
4. DH and NJ to make sure captioning is booked for any future meeting with Keziah, including the next annual review.
5. KF to update the vehicle details in the staff portal if the nominated vehicle changes.

8. Employee response

Keziah read this note in draft and agreed it is accurate. She asked that the wording about her brother be kept as brief as possible. The wording above reflects that request. She asked for nothing further and thanked Dominic for backing her.

Queries about access to or correction of this file go to privacy@kestrelplainshealth.example, attention the Privacy Officer.

Nina Josko
HR Business Partner, People and Culture
ni.josko@kestrelplainshealth.example

text:
Tuartglen Engineering Consultants
Internal Quality and Field Safety Review: Document Control, Plant Inspection and Site Access
Report reference: TEC/QA/2026/031
Issue date: 22 April 2026
Classification: Internal, for distribution to the Executive Committee and practice leads

Document control

Prepared by: Quality and Compliance Manager
Reviewed by: Health, Safety and Environment Lead
Approved by: Managing Director
Revision: B (supersedes Revision A, issued for comment on 8 April 2026)

1. Executive summary

This report records the outcome of the first-quarter internal review of document control, plant inspection and site access at the Tuartglen Perth Office and the Jarrah Point Field Office. The review was commissioned at the Executive Committee meeting of 12 February 2026. Fieldwork ran for 15 working days, starting on 2 March 2026.

Overall, the practice controls are working as designed. The review found no major nonconformities. It raised four minor findings and three opportunities for improvement. All minor findings have an owning role and a target close-out date. All but one are expected to close within 60 days of this report.

The most significant observation is about drawing transmittals for the civil and structural workstream. Superseded revisions remained in the shared project folder for longer than the 10 business days allowed by the document control procedure. No superseded drawing was issued for construction. The risk is nonetheless rated moderate because of the volume of drawings now moving through the Jarrah Point workstream.

2. Scope and method

2.1 In scope

- Document control for active projects administered from the Tuartglen Perth Office, including transmittals, revision registers and the client issue log.
- Pre-start plant inspection records for survey vehicles, drilling rigs and the elevated work platform held at the Jarrah Point Field Office.
- Visitor and contractor site access controls at both sites, including induction records kept against company accounts (not individuals) and the swipe-access zone map.

2.2 Out of scope

Financial controls, client billing and the professional indemnity insurance renewal were excluded. They are covered by the separate finance review scheduled for the second quarter.

2.3 Method

The review team was the Quality and Compliance Manager, a Senior Document Controller seconded from another workstream, and the Field Operations Coordinator. They sampled 120 drawing transmittals, 48 plant pre-start checklists and 30 days of visitor register entries. Walk-through inspections were held in Project Room Bluewater, the Plan Store Level 2 and the Field Equipment Cage at Jarrah Point. Entry and closing meetings took place in Boardroom 4.02.

3. Findings

3.1 Finding F1 (minor): superseded drawings retained in working folders

Of the 120 transmittals sampled, 14 had superseded revisions still sitting in the working folder more than 10 business days after the new revision was issued. Every case was on the coastal pipeline relocation project, change log TEC-CR-2026-0417. The current revision was correctly flagged in the register in each case. The procedure, however, requires superseded files to be moved to the archive folder. The Senior Document Controller will run a weekly sweep until the backlog is cleared, with a target close-out of 30 June 2026.

3.2 Finding F2 (minor): incomplete pre-start checklists for the elevated work platform

Five of the 18 pre-start checklists sampled for the elevated work platform had the hydraulic hose inspection line left blank. On each of those days the platform was tagged out of service for other reasons and was not used. The checklist form still does not show clearly when an item does not apply. Fleet asset EWP-0723 has been fitted with a revised checklist that adds a "not used today" box. The change will roll out across the fleet within 4 weeks of this report.

3.3 Finding F3 (minor): replacement fall-arrest anchors not yet received

The anchor points on the mezzanine of the Field Equipment Cage reached their inspection expiry during the review period and were tagged out on 9 March 2026. Replacement anchors were ordered under PO-48213, but the supplier has advised a lead time of about 6 weeks. The mezzanine stays closed until then. Items stored there have been moved to ground-level racking.

3.4 Finding F4 (minor): visitor register for client walk-throughs

Client groups visiting the Tuartglen Perth Office for design presentations are signed in as a single company entry. The access procedure requires a head count for evacuation purposes. The Office Services Supervisor has added a head-count field to the reception tablet form. This finding will close at the next evacuation drill, planned for the week of 18 May 2026.

3.5 Opportunities for improvement

OFI-1. Combine the drawing register and the client issue log into one register. This would remove the duplicate entry step that contributed to F1.

OFI-2. Schedule a joint walk-through with the landlord's facilities team for the Level 4 Comms Room. Air-conditioning alarms there were logged twice during the review period, raised under building ticket BLD-2026-1188.

OFI-3. Standardise traffic management plans for survey crews working near public foreshore areas. Recent coastal monitoring around Elizabeth Quay and the foreshore reserve at Point Walter showed that each crew prepared its own plan. A shared template would cut preparation time and keep exclusion distances consistent.

4. Corrective action register

| Ref | Finding | Owning role | Target date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Superseded drawings retained | Senior Document Controller | 30 June 2026 | Open |
| F2 | Pre-start checklist gaps | Field Operations Coordinator | 20 May 2026 | In progress |
| F3 | Fall-arrest anchors | Health, Safety and Environment Lead | 12 June 2026 | Awaiting supplier, PO-48213 |
| F4 | Visitor head count | Office Services Supervisor | 22 May 2026 | In progress |

All actions are tracked in the practice quality register under TEC/QA/2026/031. Any action that slips more than 14 days past its target date is escalated to the Managing Director.

5. Conclusion

Document control, plant inspection and site access controls are generally effective across both sites. The findings point to gaps in forms and housekeeping, not to failures of the controls themselves. Once the four corrective actions are complete, a follow-up review will verify close-out. It is provisionally scheduled within 3 months of this report, with the closing meeting set for 21 July 2026 in Boardroom 4.02.

Appendix A: Documents and records referred to

- Document Control Procedure, TEC-PRO-DC-004, Revision 7
- Plant Pre-start Inspection Procedure, TEC-PRO-HSE-012, Revision 3
- Site Access and Visitor Management Procedure, TEC-PRO-FAC-002, Revision 5
- Change log for the coastal pipeline relocation project, TEC-CR-2026-0417
- Purchase order for replacement fall-arrest anchors, PO-48213
- Purchase order for revised checklist printing, PO-48257

Appendix B: Review schedule

| Activity | Location | Date | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry meeting | Boardroom 4.02 | 2 March 2026 | 1 hour |
| Document sampling | Project Room Bluewater | 3 March 2026 to 11 March 2026 | 7 working days |
| Plant records and walk-through | Jarrah Point Field Office | 12 March 2026 to 17 March 2026 | 4 working days |
| Site access review | Tuartglen Perth Office | 18 March 2026 to 20 March 2026 | 3 working days |
| Closing meeting | Boardroom 4.02 | 23 March 2026 | 90 minutes |

Comments on this report should be sent to the Quality and Compliance Manager within 10 business days of the issue date. After that period the report will be filed as final.

text:
Kestrel Plains Health and Community Care Network
Internal Review Report

Review of Equipment Loan Tracking and Service Desk Handling for Home-Based Programs

Report reference: 48210376
Prepared by: Office of the Quality and Risk Manager
Prepared for: Clinical Governance Committee
Classification: Internal – not for external distribution
Status: Final, tabled at the committee meeting of 14 May 2026

---

1. Executive summary

This report reviews how KPCN issues, tracks and recovers clinical equipment that is loaned out under the Hospital in the Home program (PRG-CH02) and the Community Nursing Program. It also covers how equipment faults are logged with the IT and biomedical service desk. The review covered the six months from January 2026 to June 2026. It used de-identified service desk records, asset register extracts and partner account statements only. No individual patient, client or staff record was opened during the review.

Overall, the loan process works, but it relies too heavily on manual reconciliation. Three issues need action:

- Asset tags are not always scanned when equipment returns to store, so the register shows items as "on loan" after they are back on the shelf.
- Service desk tickets for home-based equipment are often logged under the wrong category, which delays routing to biomedical engineering.
- Partner client accounts are invoiced late for shared equipment. This creates reconciliation work at month end.

The review makes seven recommendations (section 5). Most can be delivered within 90 days without new funding.

2. Scope and method

In scope:
- Loan equipment held at Corella Downs Base Hospital, Redgum Point Hospital and Ironbark Crossing Community Health Centre.
- The central equipment store in the Sandstone Building and the satellite store in the Kurrajong Allied Health Building.
- Service desk tickets tagged "home equipment", "infusion pump", "pressure care" or "telemonitoring".
- Partner client accounts used for cost recovery on shared equipment.

Out of scope:
- Equipment held in residential aged-care homes. This is covered by a separate review for the Aged Care Quality Committee.
- Pharmacy-supplied consumables.
- Clinical decisions about who receives equipment.

Method:
- An extract of 412 service desk tickets was analysed by category, site, time to first response and time to resolution.
- A random sample of 60 asset records was physically checked against store shelves at each in-scope site.
- Eleven partner client accounts were reconciled against invoices raised from the finance system (cost centre 482117).
- Structured walk-throughs were held with the Nurse Unit Manager group, the Facilities Manager, an IT Service Desk Analyst and the Clinical Informatics Lead. These were process walk-throughs. Notes record the steps described, not who described them.

3. Background

The Hospital in the Home program has grown steadily since 2024. Demand for home infusion and remote monitoring has risen across the catchment. Equipment is supplied from the network's own pool and, for some items, from a shared pool funded jointly with local partners. Shared items are recharged to the partner's client account each quarter.

Loans are recorded in the asset module of the facilities system, version 4.12.3. Each item carries an asset tag in the network format, for example AST-CD-20417 for a syringe driver based at Corella Downs. When an item fails in the field, community staff raise a ticket through the service desk portal or by contacting servicedesk@kestrelplainshealth.example.

4. Findings

4.1 Return scanning

In the shelf check, 9 of the 60 sampled assets (15%) were physically in store but recorded as "on loan". In every case the return had been accepted at the counter without a scan. Counter staff described handheld scanners at the Kurrajong Allied Health Building store that are slow to wake from standby. When a queue forms, staff fall back to writing returns on paper form F-2214 and keying them in later. Some paper forms were never keyed in.

Risk: equipment appears unavailable, so additional items are hired unnecessarily. The review estimates avoidable hire costs of about $14,000 over the period.

4.2 Ticket categorisation

Of the 412 tickets, 87 (21%) were logged under "general IT" rather than "biomedical – home equipment". Misrouted tickets took a median of 2.6 working days longer to reach the correct team. Example: SD-4410732 concerned a telemonitoring hub that would not sync. It sat in the general queue for four working days before it was reassigned. SD-4415980 followed the same pattern for an infusion pump alarm fault.

The portal's category list does not mention home equipment on its first screen. Staff working in the field on a mobile device tend to choose the first plausible option.

4.3 Response times

Correctly categorised tickets met the 4-hour first-response target in 93% of cases. The resolution target of 2 working days was met in 78% of cases. Performance was weakest for tickets raised on weekends from Mallee Springs CHC, where there is no on-site biomedical cover.

4.4 Partner client account reconciliation

Of the eleven partner client accounts reviewed, eight were reconciled without variance. Three showed timing differences:

- CA-207714: two quarters invoiced together, under invoice INV-30518.
- CA-207739: a credit was not applied for equipment that was returned early.
- CA-211052: a purchase order mismatch, against order PO-771045.

None of the variances was material, but each took several hours of finance and store time to resolve.

4.5 Training and awareness

Loan procedures are not covered in the Privacy and Confidentiality Essentials module (TRN-1210). They are also not covered in any other mandatory module. New community staff learn the process on the job.

Store staff noted that the clean-up run during the Green Wards Sustainability Challenge found a backlog of unreturned items. This suggests that a recurring campaign could help.

5. Recommendations

R1. Replace or reconfigure the handheld scanners at the Kurrajong Allied Health Building store. Retire the paper fallback form within 60 days.

R2. Add "Home and community equipment" as a first-screen category in the service desk portal. Route it directly to biomedical engineering.

R3. Publish a one-page quick guide for raising equipment tickets. Circulate it through the Nurse Unit Manager group.

R4. Pilot an on-call biomedical escalation for weekend tickets from Mallee Springs CHC and Ironbark Crossing Community Health Centre for 3 months.

R5. Move partner client account recharging from quarterly to monthly. Invoices should be raised within 10 business days of month end.

R6. Add a short equipment loan segment to orientation for staff in the Community Nursing Program and the Palliative Care at Home program.

R7. Run a yearly equipment amnesty week alongside Falls Prevention Awareness Week. Pressure care and mobility items are often held over in the community at that time of year.

6. Implementation timeline

| Recommendation | Owner (role) | Target |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Facilities Manager | Within 60 days of approval |
| R2 | Clinical Informatics Lead | Before the end of August 2026 |
| R3 | Quality and Risk Manager | Within 30 days |
| R4 | Facilities Manager | 3-month pilot from September 2026 |
| R5 | Chief Financial Officer | From the October 2026 billing cycle |
| R6 | Nurse Unit Manager group | Next orientation intake |
| R7 | Quality and Risk Manager | First run in 2027 |

Progress will be reported to the Clinical Governance Committee every 6 months.

---

Appendix B – Locations of equipment stores

- Central store: ground floor, Sandstone Building, 120 Banksia Street, Corella Downs VIC 3398.
- Satellite store: Kurrajong Allied Health Building, Redgum Point Hospital.
- Overflow storage: a lockable bay next to the Spinifex Outpatients Clinic. This bay is for returns only.

MERRIGAL RIDGE HIGH OPENS NEW SCIENCE AND AGRICULTURE CENTRE AFTER TWO-YEAR DELAY

*Western Slopes Community Bulletin, Education*

Families across the district will finally get a look inside the new science and agriculture centre at Merrigal Ridge High School. The school has confirmed the building will open to the public for a community afternoon on Anzac Day weekend. The centre was first promised in 2023 and was meant to be finished within 18 months. It ended up taking almost three and a half years.

The two-storey building sits beside the Corrowong Street Agricultural Annexe, which the school has run as a working farm plot since the 1970s. It holds six laboratories, a seed and soil testing room, a small greenhouse and a lecture theatre for 120 people. Classes will move in over 3 weeks, starting from the first day of Term 2. Senior chemistry and biology go first.

The delay made regional headlines last year. In November the original builder, Danbury Kerr Constructions Pty Ltd, was ordered by the District Court to pay $1.2 million in damages over defective roofing and drainage at the site. The company had 28 days to lodge an appeal and did not do so. A second contractor, Halvorsen Brothers Building Group, took over the works in January. It finished the job with 6 weeks to spare on its revised schedule.

A school spokesperson said the community had been "extraordinarily patient". The spokesperson added that the court outcome meant the repairs had not come out of the school's own budget. "Every dollar of that settlement went back into the building," the spokesperson said.

Visitors to the community afternoon will be able to tour the laboratories and see student projects on water quality in the local creek. A short history display in the foyer will also be open. Its centrepiece is a reproduction of a nineteenth-century portrait of Caroline Chisholm, the social reformer. A small district school library in the area was once named after her. The display has been lent for 90 days by the Western Slopes Historical Society.

The opening also marks a staffing change. The school is advertising a new Head Teacher Agriculture position, and applications close within 30 days of the advertisement. A Farm Assistant role will be filled before the start of Term 3. Both positions will be based at the annexe rather than the main campus.

Parking on Corrowong Street will be limited on the day. Visitors are asked to use the oval car park off Station Road, where a shuttle will run every 15 minutes between 1 pm and 4 pm. The school canteen will be open, and the Merrigal Ridge Rural Fire Brigade will run a sausage sizzle to raise funds for its new tanker.

Further community events are planned for later in the year. These include a careers evening in Term 3 and a Remembrance Day service on 11 November 2026, which will be held for the first time in the new lecture theatre.
